title: From risk to resilience: causal evidence on the impact of foreign investment security reviews on high-tech supply chains
summary: Purpose This study examines whether foreign investment security reviews affect the supply chain resilience (SCR) of Chinese high-tech enterprises and identifies the mechanisms through which firms respond to external institutional pressure. Design/methodology/approach This study utilizes the enactment of the US Foreign Investment Risk Review Modernization Act (FIRRMA) as a quasi-natural experiment to assess its impact on the SCR of Chinese high-tech A-share listed enterprises from 2011 to 2023. Employing a double machine learning framework, the analysis provides robust causal inference and systematically explores the underlying mechanisms. Findings FIRRMA significantly enhances SCR. This improvement is primarily driven by strengthening R&D intensity, promoting digital transformation, and advancing intelligent supply chain management. The effect is more pronounced among non-state-owned enterprises, those in growth or maturity stages, and enterprises in highly competitive industries. Further analysis reveals a synergistic effect between FIRRMA and China's pilot policy for supply chain innovation and application, which amplifies the positive impact under specific conditions. Originality/value From a performance management perspective, this study shows how external institutional shocks reshape resilience-oriented performance by encouraging high-tech firms to reconfigure innovation, digital, and supply chain management capabilities.

title: CEO power and corporate social responsibility: are the strengths and concerns of CSR significant?
summary: Purpose Stakeholder theory states that the chief executive officer (CEO) invests in corporate social responsibility (CSR) to increase firm value, not because of opportunistic behavior and self-interest incentives. On the other hand, based on agency theory, increasing the CEO’s power causes a conflict between the interests of managers and shareholders. So, the CEO will have sufficient motivation to increase investment in CSR. This study examines the relationship between CEO power and CSR in listed firms on the Tehran Stock Exchange (TSE). Design/methodology/approach The authors used a KLD inspired framework adapted to the Iranian context to calculate CSR. The panel data of the 1,030 firm-year observations from companies listed on the TSE during the years 2014–2023 was adopted in this study. The data were analyzed via fixed effects regression with cluster-robust standard errors to test the research hypothesis. Findings According to agency theory, this study finds that CEO power positively affects CSR. The authors also find that CEO power positively affects CSR’s positive rating (strengths) and has no significant effect on negative rating (concerns). In other words, the CEO’s power has a distinct impact on the strengths and concerns of the company’s social responsibility. Originality/value This study contributes to the emerging literature on CEO power and CSR by providing evidence from an underexplored institutional setting and by distinguishing between CSR strengths and CSR concerns. By demonstrating that CEO power primarily drives CSR strengths rather than concerns, the study refines agency theory perspective and offers a novel contribution distinct from prior work in developed markets. The findings provide insight into the experimental test of agency versus stakeholder theory in a unique institutional context. Beyond the Iranian context, the findings suggest that the institutional environment plays a decisive role in shaping the relationship between CEO power and CSR, offering broader implications for comparative corporate governance research in emerging markets.

title: Nanotechnology Adoption, Green Innovation and ESG Performance: The Mediating Role of Environmental Accounting in Sustainable Business
summary: The growing need to reconcile technological advancement with environmental responsibility has increased attention to sustainable business practices in emerging economies such as Bangladesh. This study examines the relationships among nanotechnology adoption, green innovation, environmental accounting, and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance, with particular emphasis on the mediating role of environmental accounting. Drawing on a quantitative, cross-sectional research design, data were collected from 300 managerial and professional respondents representing technology-intensive pharmaceutical, chemical, and electronics and electrical manufacturing firms in Bangladesh. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) through SmartPLS 4.0, including measurement model assessment, structural path analysis, and bootstrapped mediation testing. The findings demonstrate that nanotechnology adoption, green innovation, and environmental accounting are positively and significantly associated with ESG performance. Environmental accounting exhibits the strongest direct relationship with ESG performance (? = 0.352, p < 0.001), while nanotechnology adoption (? = 0.280, p < 0.001) and green innovation (? = 0.191, p < 0.001) also show significant positive effects. Importantly, environmental accounting significantly mediates the relationships between nanotechnology adoption and ESG performance (? = 0.188, p < 0.001) and between green innovation and ESG performance (? = 0.201, p < 0.001). The model explains 37.3% of the variance in ESG performance and demonstrates predictive relevance. These findings highlight environmental accounting as a critical organizational mechanism for translating technology and innovation into measurable sustainability outcomes, offering practical implications for Bangladeshi firms seeking to strengthen ESG performance through responsible technological and environmental management.

title: The Effect of Tax Avoidance, Profitability, Independent Commissioners, and Audit Committee on Real Earnings Management: Evidence from Indonesian Manufacturing Companies
summary: Real earnings management reduces earnings quality and the reliability of financial reporting. This study examines the effect of tax avoidance, profitability, independent commissioners, and audit committee on real earnings management in manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024. Using a quantitative approach, this study analyzes secondary data from 61 companies (305 firm-year observations) selected through purposive sampling and employs multiple linear regression analysis. The results show that profitability has a positive and significant effect on real earnings management, whereas tax avoidance, independent commissioners, and audit committee have no significant effect. Simultaneously, all independent variables significantly influence real earnings management. These findings support Agency Theory, indicating that profitability remains the primary driver of managerial earnings management, while corporate governance mechanisms have not effectively constrained such practices. This study provides empirical evidence on the determinants of real earnings management in Indonesian manufacturing companies.

title: TURKIYE–AZERBAIJAN LOGISTICS INTEGRATION AND STRATEGIC SUPPLY CHAIN RESILIENCE
summary: Eurasian transport corridors have acquired renewed strategic importance as governments and firms seek to diversify routes and manage geopolitical, operational, and climate-related disruption. This article examines Türkiye–Azerbaijan logistics integration through the Trans-Caspian Middle Corridor, the Baku–Tbilisi–Kars (BTK) railway, and the proposed connection linking mainland Azerbaijan with Nakhchivan through Armenia, discussed in regional diplomacy through the Zangezur route and, since 2025, the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP). The study combines a qualitative, document-based case study with a conceptual synthesis of neorealist geopolitics, complex interdependence, supply-chain resilience, and dynamic capabilities. Updated institutional evidence indicates that corridor performance depends not only on the expansion of rail and port capacity but also on coordinated timetables, interoperable data, transparent tariffs, reliable Caspian shipping, and accountable cross-border governance. The World Bank’s 2026 assessment projects substantial potential gains from integrated investment and reform, while also identifying persistent infrastructure and institutional constraints. The analysis argues that the Zangezur/TRIPP connection could add network redundancy, but its contribution remains conditional on implementation, commercial viability, and agreed sovereignty-respecting customs and transit arrangements. The article concludes with a phased governance framework and measurable indicators for public authorities and private operators.

title: Resilience in the face of disruption: how supply chain innovation drives operational performance in a resource-constrained environment
summary: Purpose The article examines the relationship between supply chain innovation (SCI) and operational performance (OP), focusing on resilience in response to varying levels of supply chain disruptions within resource-constrained contexts. In the context of the dynamic capability theory, this study has sought to fill a very important gap in the literature on the SCI–OP relationship. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 697 manufacturing and service firms in Ghana using a two-phase survey. Data were analyzed using the Hayes conditional PROCESS analysis. Findings The results showed that supply chain resilience strongly mediates the relationship between innovation and OP. Furthermore, innovative practices perform significantly better in high-disruption contexts than in low-disruption contexts, thereby improving OP. Research limitations/implications Although the study employed a two-phase time-lagged survey design, the observational nature of the data limits strong causal inference, limiting the generalizability of the findings to other economies. Future research should adopt longitudinal designs and explore additional contextual variables to deepen understanding of how dynamic capabilities evolve and interact to influence OP in resource-constrained and unstable environments. Originality/value This study advances the dynamic capability perspective by positioning supply chain resilience as a mediating mechanism and contextualizing disruption as a boundary condition that strengthens the SCI–OP relationship. By focusing on Ghana, it provides novel insights from a resource-constrained, emerging economy context, highlighting how innovation and resilience interact to sustain performance amid persistent external shocks.

title: The Impact of Stock Liquidity on Corporate ESG : Which Industry Benefits?
summary: ABSTRACT Considering the role of capital market governance in guiding corporate green transformation under the goal of environmental protection, this paper aims to empirically study the impact of stock liquidity on corporate ESG based on the data of listed companies in China from 2009 to 2021. The empirical results indicate that stock liquidity exerts a positive impact on the overall corporate ESG and the three specific dimensions, such as environmental performance, social responsibility, and corporate governance. Furthermore, empirical evidence suggests that stock liquidity can positively affect the ESG performance by inducing green technology innovation and improving managerial shareholding. Finally, the results for heterogeneity indicate that stock liquidity's positive impact on corporate ESG varies among different firms, which is stronger in heavily polluting industries, competitive industries, and western regions. By alleviating the influence of stock liquidity on corporate ESG performance, this study provides certain policy implications for promoting green transformation.

title: The Impact of Accounting Conservatism on Earnings Management, the Moderating Role of Capital Ownership Structures - Empirical Evidence in Vietnam
summary: Purpose: This study aims to extend the existing literature by empirically examining the influence of accounting conservatism on earnings management in the Vietnamese context. In particular, this study also investigates how ownership structures moderate the relationship between conservative accounting and earnings management. Methodology: A multivariate regression model on a sample of 1,075 firm-year observations of 215 companies listed on HOSE or HNX from 2019 to 2023 was employed. In this study, we used panel data to test the hypotheses. Furthermore, firm size, financial leverage, and audit firm type were used as control variables. Findings: The findings shed light on the negative relationship between accounting conservatism and earnings management in the Vietnamese context. Overall, accounting conservatism still plays a positive informational role in Vietnam’s financial statements in this manner. The findings also reveal that large shareholder ownership strengthens the negative effect of accounting conservatism on earnings management, while managerial ownership and state ownership weaken this relationship. Research limitations/implications: Our findings provide important implications for companies, users of financial statements, and accounting standards setters to consider the impact of accounting conservatism on earnings management, which results in high-quality earnings reported in the financial statements. Originality/value: The study further contributes to the scholarly literature by examining whether and how ownership structures moderate the relationship between accounting conservatism and earnings management, thereby addressing the existing research gap and offering additional insights into the conflicting findings of previous research.

title: The Twin Transformation illusion: testing the limits of digital and sustainability synergy in fashion
summary: Introduction This study examines whether digital and sustainable capabilities independently and jointly influence firm performance in the global fashion industry. While prior research assumes that digital transformation and sustainability initiatives enhance competitiveness, empirical evidence on their combined effects remains limited. Methods Drawing on dynamic capabilities and institutional theory, digital capabilities are conceptualized as sensing mechanisms, whereas sustainable capabilities are framed as transforming mechanisms. The study employs a time-lagged quantitative design based on 73 publicly listed fashion firms. Capability adoption is measured using computer-assisted text analysis with syntactic dependency parsing, allowing substantive strategic actions to be distinguished from symbolic disclosures. Results Neither digital nor sustainable capabilities exhibit significant universal effects on firm performance, and no evidence of a synergistic interaction is identified. Although digital capabilities initially appear to benefit fast fashion firms under parametric estimation, this segment-specific advantage is not robust to bootstrap validation or heteroskedasticity-consistent standard errors. Sustainability initiatives show no statistically significant association with either operational performance or market valuation. The market valuation model is not significant overall; therefore, its coefficients are not interpreted. Discussion The divergence between operational performance and market valuation is consistent with a theoretical legitimacy gap, although this remains a conceptual proposition requiring further testing. Overall, the findings highlight the context-dependent nature of capability effectiveness and challenge the assumed complementarity of digital and sustainability transformation.

title: Analyzing the role of business digitization interface in the humanitarian services supply chain for community well-being
summary: Purpose This study aims to reduce the hurdles in the humanitarian services supply chain (HSSC) deliverance with digitization. This will help reduce the communication and execution gap between the participating organization, suppliers and ground-level welfare service vendors. Design/methodology/approach The hybrid Plan-Do-Check-Act–fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution approach was adapted to strategize, address and prioritize the key strategic benefits (KSBs) of using business digitization interface (BDIs) with an interactive dashboard for data visualization and efficient monitoring. Findings The HSSCs typically depend on the availability of funds, procurement of relief materials, allocation of projects, engagement of service vendors and project execution. A unique approach was adapted to visualize the HSSC using BDIs to reduce inefficiencies in conventional tender-based welfare systems and international aid for Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3, SDG7 and SDG11. Research limitations/implications The study reflects the use of data visualization in non-profit community development activities with the Technology–Organization–Environment–Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology approach. This replaces the old conventional methods of favored/non-transparent tender allotments. Non-profit organizations often lack access to funds to implement modern technology. However, adopting cost-effective, sustainable technology will pave the way for performance improvements and future adaptations. Practical implications The dashboard created with BDI enables ground-level implementation with direct source connectivity integrated with blockchain, Internet of Things and artificial intelligence. This implementation can be a digital twin that will bring resilience to HSSCs. Social implications Adapting BDIs for managerial activities will expedite welfare tasks. This study can guide the digitization of international humanitarian aid efforts if implemented. Originality/value This study addresses more philanthropic goals than corporate social responsibility objectives. Hence, this study can be replicated in relief supply chains in the regional or international landscapes.

title: The Relationship between Firm Sustainability Practices and Performance: Some Evidence from Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Australia
summary: The main aim of the research is to analyse the relationship between sustainability practices and the performance of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Australia. Although sustainability practices have received global attention, existing studies focus on large organisations, with limited empirical evidence on how SMEs adopt and benefit from these practices. This study addresses this gap by drawing on Stakeholder and the Resource-Based View (RBV) to examine, through a quantitative approach to examine how sustainability practices affect both financial and non-financial outcomes in Australian SMEs, as well as the challenges and opportunities of voluntary adoption. Survey data were collected from 322 respondents through Prolific, using a structured questionnaire developed in Qualtrics. The data are analysed using multiple regression analysis in IBM SPSS to assess the effects of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) sustainability practices on both financial and non-financial outcomes. The findings show that environmental sustainability practices have a significant positive relationship with financial performance, consistent with the RBV perspective that sustainability-driven capabilities can serve as valuable and difficult-to-imitate strategic resources that enhance competitive advantage. Furthermore, all three dimensions, i.e., environmental, social, and governance, demonstrate a significant positive association with non-financial performance, supporting Stakeholder Theory’s proposition that effective stakeholder management enhances reputational, operational, and stakeholder-related outcomes. This study contributes to the business, management, and accounting literature by providing empirical evidence from the Australian SME context. It extends research on ESG performance beyond large firms and offers practical insights for SME owners and managers on integrating sustainability practices into their operations.

title: Unlocking Supply Chain Resilience: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence and IoT Integration in Agribusiness Operations
summary: Agribusiness supply chains are exposed to climate variability, biological uncertainty, perishability, demand volatility, infrastructure constraints, and fragmented coordination among farmers, processors, traders, logistics providers, retailers, and regulators. These vulnerabilities increasingly intersect with the transition toward lower-carbon production and distribution. Artificial intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) offer complementary capabilities: connected sensors and devices can capture field, storage, processing, and transport conditions, while AI can convert heterogeneous data into forecasts, anomaly alerts, and operational recommendations. This article examines how AI–IoT integration can improve supply chain resilience and operational efficiency while supporting carbon-neutrality transitions in agribusiness. An integrative review of recent academic research and authoritative reports is used to develop a theory-informed framework. The synthesis identifies six pathways: end-to-end visibility, predictive risk sensing, adaptive planning, quality and loss control, low-carbon operational optimization, and collaborative learning. It also identifies important boundary conditions, including data quality, connectivity, interoperability, managerial capabilities, farmer participation, cybersecurity, financing, and governance. The analysis cautions that digital adoption does not automatically create resilience or sustainability: poorly designed systems can intensify dependence on vendors, exclude smallholders, optimize local efficiency at the expense of system-wide performance, or increase energy use without reducing absolute emissions. The article proposes a phased implementation model and research propositions linking AI IoT capability to resilience, efficiency, and environmental outcomes. It argues that the strategic value of smart agribusiness should be assessed through verified reductions in disruption exposure, avoidable losses, resource intensity, and emissions—not through technology deployment alone.

title: The Role of Green Human Resource Management in Shaping Corporate Social Responsibility
summary: ABSTRACT This research synthesises a decade of theoretical research on green HRM with corporate social responsibility (CSR). Green human resource management (GHRM) has emerged as a strategic lever to integrate environmental concerns into core HR functions, supporting organisations in aligning their internal practices with broader sustainability goals. The debate on green HRM and CSR seems to be fragmented and unclear in the existing literature. The systematic review and bibliometric analysis were conducted on 224 peer‐reviewed articles from 2011 to 2023. This paper adopts the Scientific Procedures and Rationales for Systematic Literature Reviews (SPAR‐4‐SLR) protocol based on performance analysis and science mapping to explore the structure, evolution, and thematic directions of GHRM. Through co‐citation and keyword co‐occurrence analyses, it identifies core clusters of knowledge and classifies research themes into motor, foundational, specialised, and emerging areas. Finally, a thematic analysis reveals the future research avenues, including the integration of digital technologies, alternative leadership models, and the psychological underpinnings of green employee behaviour. This research contributes to both academic and managerial discourse by demonstrating how GHRM serves not only as an operational human resources management practice but as a key enabler of CSR and sustainability strategies. We integrate stakeholder theory and AMO theory by considering multistakeholders' needs and expectations. This review provides a fresh perspective on the adoption of green HRM and CSR for business and society. The findings offer actionable insights for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers committed to fostering environmentally responsible and socially aligned organisations.

summary: This research aimed to examine corporate governance, liquidity management and profitability affecting investment decisions in listed companies on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in the SET ESG index, classifying investment decisions into three dimensions: earnings per share, stock price and price change rate. Secondary data were collected from financial statements, Form 56-1 One Report, the Corporate Governance Report of Thai Listed Companies, and the corporate-action adjusted stock price database during 2023–2025, comprising 62 companies and 186 firm-year observations. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis and multiple regression. As the data constitute a panel, a robustness check was additionally performed using panel regression models selected by the Hausman test with firm-clustered robust standard errors. The results revealed that profitability significantly affected investment decisions at the 0.01 level in all three dimensions (earnings per share F = 8.108, R² = 0.152; stock price F = 7.707, R² = 0.146; price change rate F = 4.981, R² = 0.099). Return on equity positively affected earnings per share and stock price, while gross profit margin positively affected earnings per share. Corporate governance affected earnings per share through board meeting frequency and stock price through board size, whereas liquidity management affected only stock price (F = 3.577, R² = 0.038). The corporate governance rating showed no significant effect because 61 of 62 companies (98.39 percent) received the highest rating. The robustness check indicated that the findings on profitability for earnings per share and price change rate, and on liquidity management for stock price, remained robust, whereas those on corporate governance and on profitability for stock price were not robust. The value of this research lies in the empirical confirmation that, even among companies with high sustainability standards, profitability and cash-conversion efficiency remain decisive factors influencing investment decisions, while also demonstrating the importance of verifying the robustness of results when using panel data. The findings benefit investors in selecting securities, executives and boards in structuring governance mechanisms and managing working capital, and regulators in refining corporate governance assessment criteria.

title: Applications of fsQCA in Logistics and Supply Chain Management: A Systematic Review
summary: Abstract Causal complexity and systems thinking have long been recognized as inherent features of logistics and supply chain management (LSCM), yet they have received limited scholarly attention, partly due to the lack of appropriate methodological tools. The emergence of fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) has reinvigorated systems thinking by introducing a configurational approach to LSCM research. Consequently, the use of fsQCA in this field has grown rapidly in recent years, warranting a systematic evaluation to support further disciplinary advancement. Drawing on a systematic review of 179 peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025, this study critically examines the application of fsQCA in LSCM. We found that fsQCA in past research was applied both as a standalone method and as a complement to conventional techniques such as regression, to identify alternative configurations of conditions for supply chain strategy, performance, sustainability, flexibility, resilience, digitalization, and collaboration. Evaluating these studies against established fsQCA methodological guidelines, the review reveals considerable inconsistencies in the analysis and reporting of data calibration, truth table construction, necessary and sufficient conditions, and robustness testing. Based on these findings, this study suggests best practice guidelines to strengthen the rigor and transparency of future configurational research and outlines agenda for advancing fsQCA-based LSCM studies. For practitioners, the configurational evidence synthesized in this review demonstrates that LSCM outcomes can be achieved through multiple distinct configurations of strategies, highlighting opportunities to adopt alternatives to one-size-fits-all best practices. The review thereby setting a benchmark to strengthen the methodological foundations for rigorous, theory-driven, and practically relevant configurational research in LSCM.

title: AI washing in corporate finance: conceptual foundations, measurement, economic consequences and future directions
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become the most attractive label in corporate strategy narratives, yet the intensity with which firms talk about AI has begun to diverge systematically from what they actually do. This phenomenon is known as AI washing. Drawing on four core empirical studies, this paper reviews the corporate finance literature on AI washing. This study develops an operational definition—a positive gap between AI Talk (disclosure) and AI Walk (substantive investment)—and delimit it against greenwashing, digital washing and impression management. This study explains why the gap pays through signalling, information asymmetry and image management, and identify cognitive dissonance as a countervailing corrective force. This study catalogues how existing work measures the construct and assess the validity of each proxy. Three outcome chains are synthesized: AI washing increases access to bank loans but not necessarily the quality of the money obtained; it has an inverted U-shaped effect on the technological gap; and it inflates investor optimism, widens analyst disagreement and raises crash risk. This study examines who can detect AI washing and conclude with seven directions for future research, arguing that the field's next step is a systematic answer to why firms wash, who believes them, who detects them, and what the practice buys against what it costs.

title: Environmental, social, governance and sales in South Korean distribution industry
summary: Purpose This study examines how environmental, social, and governance (ESG) activities influence sales performance in the South Korean distribution industry, focusing on the moderating roles of advertising intensity and firm type (wholesale vs. retail). Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from 50 publicly listed wholesale and retail firms from 2012 to 2021, fixed-effects regression models were estimated. ESG performance was measured using annual evaluation scores from the Korea Institute of Corporate Governance and Sustainability (KCGS). Findings The direct effect of ESG activities on sales was not statistically significant. However, advertising intensity strengthened the relationship between overall ESG performance and sales. When ESG dimensions were analyzed separately, only the interaction involving the social dimension showed a significant positive relationship with sales. ESG effects were also stronger for retailers than for wholesalers, suggesting that consumer-facing contexts enhance ESG effectiveness. Originality/value This study extends ESG research by focusing on short-term sales outcomes and highlighting the roles of ESG heterogeneity, communication, and firm type in shaping ESG effectiveness.

title: The Influence Of Environmental Performance And Corporate Governance On Earnings Quality In Coal Mining Companies Listed On The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX)
summary: This study examines the impact of environmental performance and the implementation of effective corporate governance principles on earnings quality in coal mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2020–2024 period. Research data were collected from sustainability reports, annual reports, and PROPER ratings, and analyzed using WarpPLS 8.0 software. The results indicate that environmental performance does not have a significant relationship with earnings quality. In contrast, the implementation of Good Corporate Governance (GCG) demonstrates a significant positive effect on enhancing earnings quality. These findings underscore the crucial role of corporate governance mechanisms in ensuring the reliability of financial reporting. To achieve more comprehensive and representative results, future research is recommended to employ alternative indicators for measuring environmental performance and to expand the study’s sample scope.

title: Effects of Financial Distress, Managerial Ownership, Institutional Ownership, and Firm Size on Earnings Management
summary: This study examines the effects of financial distress, managerial ownership, institutional ownership, and firm size on earnings management in the hotels, resorts, and cruise lines subsector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2022–2024. The research is motivated by discrepancies between operating activity and earnings growth during post-pandemic economic fluctuations, including rising profits despite declining operating revenue at PT Eastparc Hotel Tbk. A quantitative approach was employed, using purposive sampling to select 18 companies from a population of 30, yielding 54 company-year observations. Earnings management was measured using the Modified Jones Model, financial distress using the modified Altman Z-score, ownership variables using shareholding proportions, and firm size using the natural logarithm of total sales. Panel data regression was performed in EViews, with the Chow and Hausman tests supporting a fixed effects specification. The reported results indicate a positive and statistically significant coefficient for financial distress, whereas managerial ownership, institutional ownership, and firm size have no statistically significant individual effects on earnings management. The model has an adjusted R-squared of 0.530608. The study interprets the financial distress finding through the debt covenant hypothesis and highlights the limited explanatory role of ownership and firm size in this setting. Future research is encouraged to distinguish distress categories explicitly and consider total assets as a more stable measure of firm size.

title: Human-in-the-Loop AI for resilient supply chain operations: a framework for augmented decision-making and ethical deployment
summary: Purpose This research examines how Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) artificial intelligence (AI) can support resilient decision-making, operational performance, transparency, trust and ethical accountability in operations and supply chain management (OSCM). Design/methodology/approach The research adopts a design science research approach combined with comparative case analysis. A HITL AI framework, termed the adaptive oversight architecture (AOA), was developed and evaluated in two contrasting OSCM contexts. System logs, operational observations, interviews and performance indicators were analysed to examine decision outcomes, human oversight, trust and accountability. Findings HITL integration was associated with improved exception-handling accuracy, reduced human override frequency, shorter task-completion times and higher user satisfaction across the two cases. Qualitative findings further indicate that trust calibration, training, interface design, workflow integration and organizational governance influence how effectively human oversight operates. The findings also identify risks of automation dependence, accountability diffusion and inappropriate reliance on algorithmic recommendations. Research limitations/implications The research is limited to two case firms, which constrains the generalizability of the findings. While the dual-case approach provides in-depth insights, broader studies involving larger datasets or cross-industry comparisons are needed to validate the proposed framework. Future research could extend the empirical base by employing longitudinal analysis, simulations or hybrid models that test HITL effectiveness under different operational conditions. These directions will allow for a more comprehensive understanding of the scalability, adaptability and long-term organizational impacts of HITL-enabled supply chains. Practical implications For practitioners, the research highlights how HITL can be implemented to strengthen supply chain decision-making while ensuring compliance with ethical and regulatory standards. It suggests that organizations should prioritize training programs, design user-friendly interfaces and establish override mechanisms to maximize HITL effectiveness. The findings emphasize the importance of aligning AI investments with human oversight structures, rather than pursuing automation in isolation. Managers can use the framework to evaluate readiness, map decision tasks suitable for HITL integration and design workflows that balance speed, transparency and accountability. Social implications By positioning humans as active collaborators, HITL contributes to responsible AI adoption that safeguards jobs, reinforces accountability and reduces risks of algorithmic bias in supply chain operations. The approach ensures that technology complements rather than replaces human expertise, fostering inclusive digital transformation. From a societal perspective, embedding ethical safeguards into AI decision-making promotes trust in enterprise systems and enhances their legitimacy. The findings encourage the development of AI solutions that not only drive operational efficiency but also align with broader social values of fairness, responsibility and human dignity. Originality/value This research conceptualizes HITL as a dynamic socio-technical arrangement rather than a static control mechanism. The proposed AOA explains how human authority, algorithmic decision-making and organizational governance interact through oversight, trust calibration and distributed accountability, providing a mechanism-based conceptualization of HITL for OSCM.

title: Blockchain Technology in Supply Chain Auditing: Enhancing Transparency and Reducing Information Asymmetry in Accounting Systems
summary: This article examines how blockchain technology may improve supply-chain auditing by strengthening traceability, evidential integrity, and the timeliness of accounting information while reducing information asymmetry among suppliers, focal firms, auditors, lenders, and investors. It develops an accounting-centered framework that distinguishes the technical immutability of recorded transactions from the reliability of the underlying events. Blockchain can create a shared, time-stamped record of inventory movements and related documents, but it cannot independently establish whether goods exist, quantities are accurate, or source data are truthful. Drawing on agency theory, information asymmetry, transaction cost economics, institutional theory, and the audit evidence framework, the article synthesizes recent research and professional guidance and proposes a testable model linking blockchain-enabled auditability to inventory audit quality and financial reporting transparency. The model treats data governance, system interoperability, internal controls, assurance design, and supplier participation as boundary conditions. It also identifies costs and risks, including implementation expense, privacy constraints, cyber vulnerabilities, oracle problems, consensus governance, and the danger of automating flawed processes. The methodological contribution is a replicable panel and field-study design with operational measures for inventory discrepancies, audit adjustments, audit effort, reporting timeliness, and disclosure quality. Because no original firm-level dataset or field experiment was supplied, the article does not report fabricated statistical estimates. Instead, it presents an evidence-based synthesis, hypotheses, implementation implications, and a research agenda for accounting and financial-technology scholarship.

title: THE LEVEL OF DEMAND FOR DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AMONG SMALL BUSINESSES AND THE KEY CHALLENGES
summary: This study examines the level of demand for digital transformation among small businesses and identifies the key challenges associated with its implementation. Digital transformation is regarded as an important factor in enhancing business efficiency, optimizing operational costs, strengthening competitiveness, and adapting to evolving market conditions. The study explores the role of digital technologies, including electronic payment systems, e-commerce platforms, cloud computing, customer relationship management (CRM) systems, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and data analytics tools, in improving the operational performance of small businesses. Particular attention is given to the financial, technological, informational, and institutional factors influencing digital transformation. These include access to financial resources, the development of digital literacy, the availability of technological infrastructure, financing opportunities, and the provision of qualified specialists. The study also emphasizes the importance of institutional reforms, government support programmes, tax incentives, and improved lending mechanisms in facilitating the digital development of small businesses. Special consideration is given to the development of the trade and information and communication technology (ICT) sectors at both the national level and in Samarkand Region. The study highlights that successful digital transformation requires not only access to digital technologies but also their effective integration into core business processes, the enhancement of managerial competencies, and the establishment of a supportive institutional environment. Strengthening these areas can contribute to the sustainable development, increased productivity, and improved competitiveness of small businesses within the evolving digital economy.

title: Factors Affecting Audit Delay
summary: Purpose: This study aims to examine the effects of firm size, profitability, solvency, and audit committee characteristics on audit delay in manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX).Methodology: This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data from audited annual financial reports of manufacturing companies during the 2021–2024 period. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 144 companies with 576 firm-year observations. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, classical assumption tests, and multiple linear regression analysis with Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS).Results: The findings show that firm size and profitability have a negative and significant effect on audit delay, indicating that larger and more profitable companies tend to complete audit processes faster. Meanwhile, solvency and audit committee characteristics do not significantly influence audit delay.Conclusion: The study concludes that company resources and financial performance play important roles in improving audit timeliness, while debt structure and audit committee size alone are insufficient to reduce audit delays.Limitation: This study is limited to manufacturing companies listed on the IDX and the explanatory power of the model, suggesting that other factors may contribute to audit delay.Contribution: This study contributes empirical evidence regarding audit delay determinants by highlighting the importance of firm characteristics and governance mechanisms in improving financial reporting timeliness.

title: Intercultural–AI Synergies for Supply Chain Resilience: A Bibliometric and Topic Modeling Review of Global Systems Research (2000–2025)
summary: Supply chain resilience has become a critical capability for organizations operating in increasingly volatile global environments, where disruptions propagate rapidly across interconnected economic, technological, and cultural systems. Although artificial intelligence (AI) and intercultural competence are both recognized as strategic enablers of resilient supply chains, research examining their combined systemic impact remains fragmented. This study provides an integrated bibliometric and topic-modeling review of the literature addressing the intersection of intercultural competence, artificial intelligence, and supply chain resilience. Using bibliographic data retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus, we analyze scientific production, collaboration networks, conceptual clusters, and thematic trajectories through Biblioshiny and SciMAT. To capture emerging conceptual patterns, we apply LDA topic modeling, which identifies 35 latent topics subsequently organized into four higher-order macroclusters: Global Risk Systems, AI-Enabled Resilience and Predictive Systems, Human and Organizational Capabilities, and Supply Chain Resilience and Sustainable Global Operations. Results indicate a growing convergence between organizational capabilities, artificial intelligence technologies, and resilience-oriented supply chain research. While AI and resilience emerge as dominant empirical themes across the dataset, intercultural competence appears primarily as an emerging conceptual dimension associated with global coordination, cross-border collaboration, and technology adoption in multicultural environments. Accordingly, the present study interprets intercultural competence as a complementary organizational layer that may support the implementation and effectiveness of AI-enabled resilience strategies within global supply chains.

title: Enterprise digitalization capability and supply chain viability: a configurational perspective on inter-firm collaboration and governance
summary: Purpose Manufacturing supply chains face recurrent disruptions that demand rapid response and recovery, as well as sustained coordination across interdependent firms. Firms often encounter difficulties in translating digital investments into broader supply chain viability (SCV) because digital capabilities must be coordinated and deployed across organizational boundaries. This study adopts SCV as an overarching analytical perspective rather than as a measured higher-order construct. It examines how enterprise digitalization capability (EDC) translates through inter-firm digital collaboration effectiveness (IDCE) into three separately modeled viability-related outcomes: supply chain agility, resilience, and sustainability. It also examines whether relationship governance (RGM) strengthens this cross-organizational deployment process. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 380 managers at manufacturing firms in China were analyzed using a complementary three-stage design. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to test the hypothesized direct, mediating, and moderating relationships. Necessary condition analysis was used to identify potential bottlenecks, while fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis identified alternative combinations of conditions associated with high outcome levels. Findings Among the sampled Chinese manufacturing firms, EDC is positively associated with IDCE, which serves as the key mechanism through which digital capabilities are translated into supply chain agility, resilience, and sustainability. RGM strengthens this capability-deployment process by enhancing the conversion of EDC into IDCE. The complementary analyses indicate that the three separately analyzed outcomes involve distinct bottleneck conditions and can be achieved through multiple configurations of digital capabilities, collaboration, and governance. Originality/value This study reframes enterprise digitalization from capability possession to cross-boundary capability deployment. By combining net-effect, necessary-condition, and configurational perspectives, it advances understanding of how distinct viability-related supply chain outcomes emerge from interactions among technological, collaborative, and relational conditions, without treating SCV as a measured aggregate construct.

title: Artificial intelligence and digital transformation for sustainable supply chain performance
summary: This study examines the nexus between digital technology adoption and Sustainable Supply Chain Management, focusing on their combined impact on sustainability performance. By bridging the domains of digital transformation and sustainability, the research advances a comprehensive conceptual framework that captures the effects of Industry 4.0 technologies, specifically the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, and blockchain, on sustainable supply chain outcomes. The proposed model posits that digital technology adoption enhances sustainability performance indirectly through improved supply chain transparency, with this relationship moderated by the presence of a skilled workforce. Grounded in a thorough review of contemporary literature, the study highlights the role of Industry 4.0 technologies in promoting eco-efficient production and logistics, the contribution of blockchain to strengthening transparency, and the optimization of resource utilization through AI. An empirical quantitative study based on survey data collected from 250 manufacturing firms provides evidence of the partial mediation effect of transparency and validates the moderating influence of human capital in reinforcing the relationship between digital transformation and sustainability. The findings offer novel theoretical insights into the mechanisms linking digital adoption to SSCM and yield practical implications for managers seeking to leverage Industry 4.0 technologies for sustainability objectives. The paper concludes by outlining directions for future research to further advance the digital–sustainability interface.

title: Data Spaces and Privacy-Preserving Computing for Cross-Border Supply Chain Collaboration: Firm Adoption, Collaboration Performance, and Trust Mechanisms
summary: The increasing complexity and data intensity of cross-border supply chains necessitate advanced solutions for secure and interoperable data sharing. This research investigates the influence of Data Spaces and privacy-preserving computing (PPC) technologies on firm adoption, collaboration performance, and trust mechanisms within these intricate networks. Addressing the limitations of traditional data sharing models, this study examines how decentralized data governance frameworks like Data Spaces, combined with PPC techniques such as homomorphic encryption and differential privacy, can foster secure and sovereign data exchange. The research identifies key drivers and barriers to the adoption of these innovative technologies, assessing their tangible impact on collaboration performance metrics including efficiency, responsiveness, and resilience. Furthermore, it scrutinizes how the inherent security and data sovereignty features of Data Spaces and PPC contribute to building and sustaining trust among disparate supply chain partners. Findings reveal critical success factors for adoption and provide quantitative evidence of performance enhancements. The study also elucidates the nuanced relationship between technological choices and trust development, culminating in a proposed framework that integrates Data Spaces, PPC, and trust mechanisms to guide organizations in achieving more effective and secure cross-border supply chain collaborations. This work offers a novel perspective on leveraging emerging technologies to overcome persistent challenges in global supply chain management.

title: From Climate-Finance Approval to Measurable Resilience in Latin America and the Caribbean: Dynamic Panel Evidence and Small-Sample Robustness
summary: Multilateral climate-finance approvals may support resilience, but approval, disbursement, execution, and measurable national outcomes occur at different stages. This study examines associations between country-specific multilateral approvals and climate vulnerability in a 20-country Latin American and Caribbean panel for 1995–2024. The preferred dynamic two-way fixed-effects models use 333 observations from 18 countries during 2006–2024, common samples, Driscoll–Kraay inference, wild cluster bootstrap tests, and a half-panel jackknife. To avoid mechanical overlap, total finance is first estimated alone and then decomposed into mutually exclusive adaptation and other-finance components. Total approvals are statistically imprecise. The component model also produces imprecise estimates until controls and institutional interactions are added; in that specification, adaptation finance and its interaction are positive, but the adaptation coefficient weakens under wild cluster inference, and both terms lose precision after jackknife correction. Results are stable to alternative starting years, bandwidths, and 20-country models that omit the controls responsible for missingness. Vulnerability remains strongly persistent. The findings do not demonstrate that climate finance is ineffective; they show that annual approval commitments, especially when sparse and upstream from implementation, cannot reliably identify realized resilience effects at the national level.

title: Research on the spatiotemporal prediction of supply chain finance risk contagion based on a dynamic graph attention diffusion mechanism
summary: This study focuses on the spatiotemporal prediction of supply chain finance risk contagion and constructs a model based on the dynamic graph attention diffusion mechanism for in-depth exploration. The risk-aware dynamic graph attention network (DyGAT) is used to model the time-varying network structure of supply chain finance, where the spatial attention weight α_ij(t) is updated adaptively at each time step by integrating real-time risk intensity signals to realize real spatiotemporal coupling modeling. A bounded diffusion mechanism with natural risk attenuation is introduced to characterize the propagation process of risks in spatial and temporal dimensions, avoiding unbounded cumulative defects in traditional formulas. Methodologically, a supply chain finance dynamic graph structure is constructed by integrating multisource data such as historical transaction data and corporate financial information, with clear data cleaning, fusion and feature engineering processes, and the model is trained, validated and ablated strictly. The results show that the model can effectively predict the spatiotemporal paths and topological characteristics of supply chain finance risk contagion and identify key nodes and critical periods of risk propagation, and the ablation experiment verifies that the dynamic attention module and bounded diffusion module bring 18.2% and 12.5% precision improvement, respectively. It provides strong support for financial institutions and supply chain enterprises to formulate risk prevention strategies in advance and is of great significance for improving the stability and resilience of the supply chain finance system. However, caution is needed when applying the model to small-sample settings, as the limited sample size may constrain its generalizability to other industries and regions.

title: Effects Of Corporate Governance and Financial Leverage of Quoted Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria
summary: This study examines the effect of corporate governance mechanisms on the financial leverage of quoted Deposit Money Banks (DMBs) in Nigeria over the period 2015–2025. Specifically, it investigates the influence of board size, board independence, board composition, gender diversity, and age diversity on leverage levels of listed commercial banks in Nigeria. The study employs a descriptive research design using panel data from 15 quoted DMBs listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group over eleven years (2015–2025). Secondary data were extracted from the annual reports and accounts of the sampled banks. Panel regression models (fixed and random effects) were utilized for data analysis, with the Hausman test applied to determine the most appropriate model specification. Diagnostic tests for heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, and multicollinearity were also conducted. The empirical findings reveal that board size has a significant and positive effect on financial leverage (debt-to-equity ratio) at β = 0.1069 (P-value = 0.0028), consistent with the agency theory perspective that larger boards may facilitate greater debt utilization. Board independence also demonstrates a significant and positive effect on the debt-to-equity ratio at β = 0.0157 (P-value = 0.0000). Furthermore, gender diversity (β = 10.5572; P-value = 0.0000) and age diversity (β = 0.0741; P-value = 0.0132) are found to have significant positive effects on leverage decisions, suggesting that diverse boards are better equipped to assess and manage financial risks. The findings support the Trade-Off Theory, indicating that while high leverage may reduce performance, strong governance mechanisms can mitigate its negative effects. The study provides valuable insights for policymakers, regulators, bank executives, and investors regarding the governance-leverage nexus in the Nigerian banking industry. It extends previous research by incorporating recent data (2015–2025) and multiple governance variables, offering contemporary empirical evidence on the governance-leverage relationship in the Nigerian banking sector during a period of significant regulatory reforms and recapitalization efforts.

title: Sea Cucumber Farming and Sasi Tradition: Synergy Between Corporate Social Responsibility and Local Wisdom in Supporting the Conservation of Natural Resources by the Ambel Indigenous Community in Raja Ampat
summary: Sasi represents a form of local wisdom among the people of Raja Ampat for regulating the use of marine resources by managing access to benefits within specific areas or timeframes. However, ensuring the sustainability of its implementation requires overcoming various challenges, thus requiring an approach that supports both conservation and the community’s utilization of natural resources. This study aims to analyze the implementation of the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) program by PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Refinery Unit (RU) Kasim through the development of sea cucumber aquaculture cages in Waifoi Village, Raja Ampat, and its contribution to the sustainability of community-based natural resource management. The study employed a case study design, with data collected through participatory observation, in-depth interviews, and focus group discussions (FGD). Informants were selected through purposive sampling, taking into account the knowledge and involvement of KTH Waifoi members in the program’s implementation. Data were analyzed descriptively to determine the program’s relevance to the sasi tradition. The results indicate that the sea cucumber aquaculture CSR program aligns with the values of the sasi tradition and supports natural resource management and conservation efforts, particularly regarding sea cucumbers in Waifoi Village

title: Digital economy-driven resilience enhancement in the global food supply chain
summary: The global food system is undergoing significant changes due to the digital economy, but the specific impact of this on the resilience of the food supply chain remains unclear. This study examines the impact of the digital economy on the resilience of food supply chains in 106 countries between 2013 and 2023. The findings show that although the digital economy is growing internationally, its development is still unequal, especially in terms of digital market and digital governance. Food trade networks are becoming more interconnected; trade in plant-based foods is more geographically diverse, while trade in animal-based foods is more closely linked. Resilience patterns reveal significant disparities, with high-income countries continuing to have a distinct edge. For animal-based food supply chains, digital technology is the main source of resilience (35.6% of total feature importance); for plant-based food supply chains, on the other hand, GDP is the most important factor (54.2%). The degree to which different digital economy factors affect resilience is determined by threshold effects. Critical levels usually fall between 36 and 74 on the digital economy index, depending on the food type and digital dimension. These results highlight the necessity of category-specific approaches to help create more resilient and sustainable global food supply chains.

title: DIGITAL FORENSIC ACCOUNTING: INTEGRATING DIGITAL EVIDENCE, ADVANCED ANALYTICS AND PROFESSIONAL JUDGEMENT FOR FRAUD DETECTION AND FINANCIAL INTEGRITY
summary: The fast growth of digital technology in financial systems has changed the nature of financial fraud. This has created new problems for traditional methods of accounting, auditing and investigation. Because of this, digital forensic accounting has become more important. It is a multidisciplinary approach that combines accounting knowledge, investigative methods, digital forensics and advanced technologies. This study examines the role of digital forensic accounting in fraud detection, financial investigation and financial integrity. It uses a conceptual and narrative review of academic literature, professional reports and reliable sources. The review shows that digital evidence, data analytics, artificial intelligence and machine learning can help identify suspicious transactions. These tools can also help examine financial data and trace financial activities. Digital forensic accounting supports fraud prevention, internal controls, transparency, accountability and corporate governance. However, technological complexity, privacy concerns, legal and ethical issues and the need for specialised skills remain important challenges.

title: Firm Characteristics and Financial Reporting Quality among Listed Non-Financial Companies in Nigeria
summary: The series of corporate failures and reporting irregularities, despite the full adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards, has raised concerns about factors affecting financial reporting quality in Nigeria This study investigated the relationship between firm attributes and financial reporting quality among 85 listed non-financial companies in Nigeria over the period 2016–2025. Financial reporting quality was examined through an income-smoothing index, with auditor type, sustainability disclosure practices and board financial expertise as the principal explanatory variables, with firm size as a control. The reported robust regression results indicated positive and statistically significant associations for auditor type and board financial expertise. Under the interpretation of the index adopted in the manuscript, these findings are consistent with lower income smoothing among firms with the relevant audit and board characteristics. In contrast, sustainability disclosure practices showed a positive but statistically non-significant association, providing insufficient evidence of a relationship within the estimated model. Firm size also demonstrated a positive and significant coefficient. External audit arrangements and board-level financial competence therefore warrant attention. Accordingly, listed companies should apply appropriate professional criteria when selecting external auditors and consider the financial expertise available within their boards. Sustainability disclosure practices may also be integrated with financial reporting processes, although their statistical association with income smoothing was not established in this study. These findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.

title: Analysis the effect of digital economy on income inequality: A study on six ASEAN countries
summary: The rapid development of the digital economy has reshaped labor markets and income distribution, raising concerns over whether digitalization exacerbates or reduces income inequality. While technological progress is often associated with skill-biased effects, digital technologies may also broaden access to markets, information, and economic opportunities, particularly in developing regions such as ASEAN. This study examines the impact of digital economy on income inequality in ASEAN countries and assesses whether the relationship follows a non-linear (U-shaped) pattern. Using panel data from six ASEAN countries (Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, and Philippines) over the period 2010–2020 (66 country-year observations), the analysis employs fixed-effects panel regression models. A quadratic specification is estimated to test for non-linearity, and potential endogeneity is addressed using a two-stage least squares (2SLS) approach with telecommunication-based instrumental variables. The empirical results indicate that digital economy has a negative and statistically significant effect on income inequality, suggesting an equalizing impact across ASEAN countries. The findings imply that digitalization reduces income inequality by expanding access to digital infrastructure and economic participation, thereby enhancing labor market inclusion and income opportunities for low- and middle-income groups. However, no robust evidence of a non-linear (U-shaped) relationship is found, as the estimated turning point lies outside the observed data range.

title: The Effect Of Green Accounting, CGPI, And Business Strategy On Value Creation Moderated By Business Model
summary: This study examines the effect of green accounting, the Corporate Governance Perception Index (CGPI), and business strategy on creating value with business model also tested as a moderating variabel. Using a quantitative explanatory research design, the study analyzes 75 panel data observations from food and beverage manufacturinng companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020-2024. Data were obtained from annual reports, sustainability reports, CGPI publication, and financial statements. Panel regression with the Fixed Effect Model and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) was employed. The results show that green accounting, CGPI, and business strategy each have a significant positive effect on creating value. Furthermore, business model strengthens the influence of both green accounting and CGPI on creating value. These findinngs highlight the importance of integrating sustainability practices, strong governance, and strategic orientation to enhance long-term corporate value.

title: Sustainable human-robot services: ESG, diversity, and attractiveness in job pursuit
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how attractiveness factors (job, organization, individual) and environmental, social and governance (ESG) aspects influence job pursuit intentions in hospitality’s human-robot collaborative environments. It investigates relationships between these factors and job pursuit intention. Design/methodology/approach The study combines mixed methods using generalized linear modeling (GLM) with Student’s t distribution and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA). Data was collected via online survey from 492 US hospitality job seekers through Amazon’s Mechanical Turk (MTurk). The research applies complexity theory to uncover nonlinear relationships and multiple pathways to outcomes. Findings GLM results show organization attractiveness, individual interest and perceived ESG environmental and governance factors significantly predict job pursuit intention. Notably, while GLM showed job attractiveness and perceived ESG social factors as insignificant individual predictors, fsQCA revealed their critical roles within specific causal configurations. Practical implications Organizations should enhance employer branding and clearly communicate their environmental and governance ESG initiatives. Companies need targeted approaches emphasizing sustainability and governance practices, while preparing employees for human-robot collaboration (HRC) through training programs highlighting growth opportunities rather than job displacement. Originality/value This research uniquely examines employee perspectives on HRC in hospitality, addressing a gap focused predominantly on consumer reactions. It integrates attractiveness factors with ESG aspects using complexity theory and fsQCA methodology.

title: Analysis of Big Data-Based Financial Technology and AI on Financial Inclusion in Indonesia
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of implementing Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based financial technology on increasing financial inclusion in Indonesia during the period 2019–2024. The background of this study is based on the rapid increase in digital transformation in the financial sector triggered by the adoption of fintech, but there is still a gap in financial access, especially among low-income groups and disadvantaged regions. This study uses a quantitative approach with a panel data model, involving independent variables of Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP), education level, average internet access, fintech loan recipient entities, and the number of mobile banking users on the dependent variable of the Financial Inclusion Index. The data was obtained from official publications of the Financial Services Authority (OJK), Bank Indonesia (BI), and the Central Statistics Agency (BPS). The results of the analysis show that Big Data and AI have a positive and significant contribution to expanding financial inclusion through increased credit distribution efficiency, expanded access to digital services, and personalized financial products. However, their influence is still limited by gaps in digital literacy, infrastructure, and trust in data security. The findings of this study are expected to provide strategic input for regulators, fintech industry players, and academics in formulating technology-based inclusive policies to achieve sustainable national financial inclusion targets.

title: Multimodal Antiemetic Prophylaxis in Patients Undergoing Endoscopic Sleeve Gastroplasty: A Single-Center Retrospective Case Series
summary: Background: Endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (ESG) is associated with a high incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) due to gastric volume reduction, preservation of vagal innervation, and inherent patient-related risk factors. Standard antiemetic prophylactic regimens are frequently insufficient in this population. This case series describes the clinical experience and postoperative outcomes associated with a multimodal antiemetic prophylaxis regimen. Methods: In this single-center retrospective case series, data from 20 adult patients who underwent ESG under general anesthesia were analyzed. Anesthesia maintenance was standardized using manually controlled intravenous infusions of propofol and remifentanil (TIVA), without volatile anesthetics. Multimodal antiemetic prophylaxis consisted of intravenous granisetron (3 mg), dexamethasone (8 mg), haloperidol (1 mg at induction + 1 mg before emergence), and fosaprepitant (150 mg). Postoperative analgesia was managed primarily with paracetamol and ibuprofen. The primary outcome was clinically documented PONV during the early postoperative period, including the PACU stay and the first 12 postoperative hours. Emergency department presentations for severe PONV within 5 postoperative days were assessed as a secondary outcome using institutional electronic health records. Results: The cohort comprised 20 patients (70% female, mean age 41.05 ± 11.22 years, mean BMI 38.33 ± 4.94 kg/m 2 ). Comorbidities were present in 55% of patients, and 80% were non-smokers. During the early postoperative period, no clinically documented episodes of PONV requiring rescue antiemetic treatment were identified. Conclusion: In this small retrospective case series, multimodal antiemetic prophylaxis combined with TIVA was associated with no institutionally documented early postoperative PONV presentations and emergency department presentations for severe PONV within 5 days after ESG. Prospective studies with standardized postoperative PONV assessment are needed to determine the efficacy of this approach. Given the limitations of a retrospective case series, prospective controlled trials incorporating systematic PONV severity scoring are warranted to establish optimized guidelines.

title: Energy-saving and emission-reduction fiscal policy and green innovation in high-emission firms: a quasi-natural experiment from China
summary: The Energy-Saving and Emission-Reduction Fiscal Policy Comprehensive Demonstration Cities program represents a targeted green policy instrument and serves as an important policy initiative for advancing China’s carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals. Using the implementation of this pilot program as a quasi-natural experiment, this study examines the impact of the policy on corporate green innovation based on a sample of listed firms in high-emission industries in China from 2007 to 2024. Employing a multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) model, we find that the Energy-Saving and Emission-Reduction Fiscal Policy significantly promotes corporate green innovation. The mechanism analysis further indicates that the alleviation of financing constraints and the optimization of human capital structure may serve as important mechanisms through which the ESER fiscal policy promotes corporate green innovation. Meanwhile, environmental regulation exerts a negative moderating effect on this relationship. Further analysis demonstrates that the positive effect of the policy on green innovation is more pronounced among large-scale enterprises, firms located in central cities, and firms in regions with stronger fiscal capacity. This study provides empirical evidence on the micro-level innovation effects of green fiscal policies and identifies the boundary conditions under which such policies influence corporate green innovation.

title: Digital Transformation in Human Resource Management among Vietnamese SMEs
summary: Digital transformation is reshaping human resource management, yet evidence on how extensively digital technologies are integrated across core human resource management functions in small and medium-sized enterprises remains limited. This study aims to examine the extent of digital transformation in human resource management among Vietnamese SMEs across four core functions: recruitment, training and development, compensation and benefits, and performance management. Data were collected through a structured survey of managers in Vietnamese small and medium-sized enterprises using stratified random sampling. After data screening, 248 valid responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics in SPSS 28.0. The findings indicate that the overall level of digital transformation in human resource management is relatively high, with an overall mean of 3.816 on a five-point scale. Training and development records the highest level of digital adoption, followed by compensation and benefits and recruitment. Performance management has the lowest level of digital transformation. These findings suggest that enterprises have progressed further in digitizing standardized human resource activities than functions requiring stronger data integration, systematic measurement, and advanced decision support. The study highlights the need for small and medium-sized enterprises to move beyond isolated digital tools toward integrated human resource management systems that connect technology, data, processes, and managerial capabilities. Future research should examine the organizational and technological factors influencing digital transformation and assess its effects on human resource and business performance.
