title: Green Accounting Disclosure and Investor Valuation: The Moderating Role of Corporate Governance in Publicly Listed Coal Sectors
summary: This article examines whether green accounting disclosure is associated with investor valuation in publicly listed coal-sector companies and whether corporate governance strengthens that relationship. Coal companies face a distinctive valuation problem: environmental information may help investors assess future liabilities, transition exposure, operating resilience, and management credibility, yet disclosure can also reveal costly environmental impacts and expose inconsistencies between stated commitments and actual performance. Building on agency, stakeholder, legitimacy, signaling, and voluntary-disclosure perspectives, the article develops a framework that separates the breadth of environmental disclosure from its quality, financial materiality, and verification. Corporate governance is conceptualized through board independence and expertise, audit committee effectiveness, ownership oversight, and the integration of climate risk into board-level risk management. A structured synthesis of recent empirical literature and official reporting frameworks is combined with a replicable panel-data design for listed coal companies. The synthesis indicates that disclosure is unlikely to produce a uniform valuation premium: investors are more likely to respond positively when information is comparable, decision-useful, credible, and linked to financial exposure, while high emissions or weak environmental performance may still be priced negatively. Effective governance can strengthen credibility and reduce managerial discretion over selective reporting, but formal governance structures alone may not ensure substantive oversight. Because no original company-year dataset is estimated in this manuscript, it does not invent coefficients or claim new causal findings. Instead, it identifies testable hypotheses, operational measures, econometric specifications, and robustness checks for an empirical study of publicly listed coal companies, with particular relevance to emerging markets such as Indonesia.

title: Collaboration of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), Village-Owned Enterprises (BUMDes), and Community Groups in Promoting Rural Development through Welfare and Environmental Improvement in Kalibaru Village, Cirebon
summary: This study analyzes multi-stakeholder collaboration in the MEGAMENDUNG Program (Mendukung Gerakan Ekonomi Desa Unggul), initiated by PT Pertamina Gas Operation West Java Area to promote sustainable development in Kalibaru Village, Cirebon Regency. This descriptive qualitative study collected data through observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation. The collaboration process was examined using Ansell and Gash’s (2008) Collaborative Governance framework, while changes in community livelihood assets were assessed using the Sustainable Livelihood Framework (Beall & Piron, 2005). The findings show that collaboration among the company, Village Government, Village-Owned Enterprise (BUMDes), community groups, and technical agencies was built through role distribution, facilitative leadership, dialogue, trust building, commitment, and shared understanding. This collaboration strengthened five livelihood assets by enhancing livestock farmers’ capacity, providing livestock infrastructure, securing land for feed cultivation, developing group institutions, improving waste management, and generating economic benefits for livestock groups. The program reduced potential emissions by 146 tons CO₂e per year, saved IDR 3.8 million per year in milk-processing costs and IDR 5 million per year in feed costs, and increased cattle sales value by up to IDR 160 million per year. These findings show the combined approach captures the program’s contribution to livelihood sustainability, community welfare, and environmental improvement.

title: Effects of Independent Commissioners, Institutional Ownership, and Audit Committees on Coal Mining Companies’ Profitability
summary: This study examines the effects of independent commissioners, institutional ownership, and audit committees on the profitability of coal mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2022–2024. The research is motivated by alleged coal mining corruption in Bengkulu involving nine suspects, eight of whom were company insiders, and estimated state losses of IDR 500 billion. These circumstances highlight the need to strengthen corporate governance so that management decisions are more accountable and support profitability. A quantitative design was employed, with purposive sampling yielding 14 eligible companies from a population of 33 and a total of 42 company-year observations. Panel data regression was conducted using EViews 12, incorporating leverage and firm size as control variables. The analysis included model selection, classical assumption tests, and hypothesis testing. The model selection procedure led to the common effects model. The results show that independent commissioners, institutional ownership, and audit committees have no statistically significant individual effects on profitability, whereas leverage and firm size have significant negative effects. The model is jointly significant and has an adjusted R-squared of 0.162660. These findings suggest that the presence or proportion of formal governance mechanisms alone does not necessarily translate into greater profitability in this industry. Future research should consider audit committee membership requirements and additional explanatory variables because most of the variation in profitability remains outside the model.

title: Accounting for otherness in social enterprise: The case of a taxation service
summary: The study aimed to account for the influence of otherness on a social enterprise's provision of tax services to clients in the Northern Territory of Australia. It collected quantitative data from client interviews conducted before the social enterprise provided taxation services. The collected useable quantitative data from 265 clients comprised 11 variables, grouped according to Role Set Theory into legal, social, and economic status roles. Nested logit regression was used to analyse the data, with roles as assigned variables for the three tax services. Results showed that neither the legal nor the social status of the otherness group significantly affected clients' willingness to obtain tax services. Economic status and the promotion of financial independence reduced the likelihood that otherness groups would obtain tax services. Including the Practitioner status of tax practitioners and the hours spent with clients in the model positively influenced tax return completion. It had a positive, significant impact on the number of females who received tax return services. However, Practitioner hours spent did not mediate the females' increased willingness to secure tax return services. This study contributes to theorising about otherness groups using Role Set Theory and presents a methodology for testing it with a nested logit regression. The study offers novel insights by investigating a relatively underexplored intersection of social enterprise, taxation services, and marginalised populations operationalised as 'otherness'. The findings are relevant for public policy, social enterprise design, and fair access to government services in underserved or remote communities.

title: Digital Transformation: Artificial Intelligence Adoption of Small Medium Enterprises in Gauteng
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is now a crucial element in the transforming of industries globally, propelled by greater development in computational processing, cloud and computational services, and deep learning technologies. Its uses, ranging from chatbots to self-driving cars, are becoming more widespread, presenting the opportunity to enhance organizational efficiency by as much as 40%. In light of global competitiveness and digital transformation, which have been induced by the COVID-19 era, AI is crucial, especially for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs). Nevertheless, SMEs face considerable obstacles to AI acceptance, such as financial and technical limitations, restricted access to advanced technologies, and a shortage of skilled personnel. These issues hinder their productivity and competitiveness within the national economy. This research investigates the elements that affect AI acceptance in the landscape of SMEs in Gauteng, with the goal of identifying barriers, evaluating the impact of managerial leadership, and assessing the use of AI in operations. A sample of 118 stakeholders, including owners, managers, and strategic employees from various backgrounds, was analysed, excluding large corporations and government entities. The study focuses on the ICT sector, exploring technological, organizational, environmental, and ethical aspects of AI implementation. The capstone report aims to formulate strategies that assist SMEs in overcoming challenges related to digital transformation, offering an introduction, literature review, methodology, analysis, and strategic recommendations specifically designed for the South African context. This research demonstrates that AI adoption among Gauteng's SMEs stands at a critical inflection point. Strong awareness of AI's potential combines with substantial adoption intentions, creating conditions for rapid diffusion. However, realising this potential requires coordinated action addressing identified barriers through organisational capability building, ecosystem enablement, and supportive policy frameworks. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Technology, Environment, Organisation, SMEs

title: Competing Through Digital Transformation in Fast Fashion: How Zara and Shein Build Competitive Advantage
summary: This study examines how digital transformation contributes to competitive advantage in the fast fashion industry through a comparative analysis of Zara and SHEIN. Although both companies have emerged as industry leaders, they pursue distinct digital transformation strategies to achieve competitive advantage. Zara relies on a vertically integrated supply chain, omnichannel retailing, and operational control to respond rapidly to changing consumer preferences, whereas SHEIN employs a digital-first business model supported by artificial intelligence, real-time data analytics, and flexible supplier networks. This study evaluates the external environment, industry dynamics, competitive positioning, internal capabilities, and the strategic alignment of both firms using established strategic management frameworks. The findings suggest that digital transformation has become a critical driver of competitiveness in the fast fashion industry by enhancing supply chain agility, market responsiveness, and customer engagement. The comparative analysis reveals that Zara’s competitive advantage is rooted in operational integration and brand recognition, while SHEIN’s advantage stems from digital agility and data-driven decision making. However, both firms face challenges related to sustainability, supply chain resilience, and regulatory pressures. This study contributes to the literature by demonstrating that firms can achieve competitive advantage in fast fashion through different digital transformation pathways, provided that digital capabilities are effectively aligned with strategic objectives, consumer expectations, and evolving market conditions.

title: Competencies and human factor-related organizational barriers to digital transformation: a systematic literature review
summary: The relationship between employee competencies and human factor-related organizational barriers remains understudied. Accordingly, this study examines how technical competencies and soft skills relate to these barriers. A systematic literature review of articles published between 2000 and 2024 and indexed in Scopus and Web of Science was conducted; 77 studies were analyzed. Three key components were identified: technical competencies, soft skills, and organizational properties. The latter may hinder or facilitate the influence of competencies, particularly soft skills, on these barriers. The results show that staff and cultural resistance are closely associated with soft skills, whereas systemic resistance is primarily linked to technical competencies. The study provides an integrative sociotechnical framework for sustainable digital transformation.

title: CORPORATE TAX PLANNING AND FINANCIAL STABILITY: THE CONTINGENT GOVERNANCE ROLE OF ESG
summary: This study empirically investigates the relationship between corporate tax planning and financial stability, highlighting the moderating role of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance. Analyzing a sample of 261 non-financial firms listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand, the research utilizes effective tax rates (ETR) and book-tax differences (BTD) to measure tax planning. Financial stability is operationalized via the Altman Z-score and Ohlson O-score. Findings reveal that BTD is significantly and positively associated with financial stability, whereas ETR exhibits no significant relationship. Crucially, moderation analysis demonstrates that strong ESG performance amplifies the positive impact of BTD on financial stability. The results suggest that BTD effectively captures complex tax-planning dimensions linked to corporate resilience. At the same time, ESG performance functions primarily as a contingent governance mechanism that enhances the credibility of these strategies. Ultimately, this research provides vital insights, indicating that the financial implications of tax planning depend substantially on a firm's broader transparency and governance environment.

title: Related Party Transactions in Promoter-Dominated Firms: Assessing the Effectiveness of Minority Shareholder Protection in India
summary: Related Party Transactions (RPTs) represent one of the most significant corporate governance challenges in jurisdictions characterized by concentrated ownership and promoter control. In India, while RPTs may facilitate legitimate business efficiencies, they also create substantial risks of tunnelling, value diversion, and expropriation of minority shareholders. Against the backdrop of recent amendments to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, this article critically examines whether the existing regulatory framework adequately safeguards minority shareholder interests in promoter-dominated firms. The study is undertaken in response to concerns that increasing reliance on audit committee oversight, evolving materiality thresholds, and procedural compliance mechanisms may weaken substantive investor protection. Using a doctrinal research methodology, the article analyses statutory provisions, regulatory developments, judicial precedents and corporate governance literature. The study finds that despite significant regulatory evolution, the Indian RPT framework remains predominantly procedural, emphasizing disclosure and approval requirements rather than substantive fairness. The absence of clear standards governing ordinary course of business, arm’s length transactions, and materiality enables regulatory arbitrage and limits the effectiveness of existing safeguards for minority shareholders. The article argues that meaningful protection of minority investors requires a shift towards a fairness-based governance model incorporating independent valuation, stronger audit committee independence, enhanced shareholder participation, and more robust enforcement mechanisms. Such reforms are essential to ensure that corporate efficiency is balanced with accountability and equitable treatment of minority shareholders.

title: Ownership Structure and Real Earning Management of Food and Beverage Companies in Vietnam: The Moderating Role of Auditing Quality
summary: This study investigates the effect of ownership structure on the real earning management (REM) of food and beverage (F&B) companies listed on the Vietnam stock market, with particular emphasis on the moderating role of auditing quality. The data employed in this study includes 138 listed F&B companies covering the period from 2022 to 2024. Using a feasible generalized least squares (FGLS) approach, the empirical findings confirm that foreign ownership and managerial ownership have significantly negative effects on REM of the F&B companies. However, this study does not find any evidence on the effect of the state ownership on the REM. Additionally, the results indicate that higher audit quality, as proxied by Big 4 auditors, is associated with lower REM. Especially, the findings show positive moderating effects of the Big 4 auditors on the relationship between ownership structure and REM, meaning that the presence of a Big 4 auditor weakens the marginal impact of ownership structure on the REM. This evidence supports the view that governance mechanisms can act as substitutes rather than complements in constraining real earning management, contributing to the broader literature on corporate governance in emerging markets. This study provides the first empirical evidence on how ownership structure influences REM within Vietnamese F&B companies. Moreover, the study offers insights into the moderating role of audit quality in the relationship between ownership structure and REM, thereby enhancing understanding of whether governance mechanisms act as substitutes or complements in constraining opportunistic behavior within transitional economies.

title: IT-Enabled Human Capital and Digital Work Environment
summary: Digital transformation in micro, small, and medium enterprises increasingly relies on information technology-enabled professionals who integrate digital systems into daily work. However, limited research explains how digital capabilities translate into individual performance within digital work systems. This study proposes a model in which the digital work environment (DWE) mediates the relationships between digital competency, fintech capability, digital leadership, and workforce performance. Partial least squares structural equation modeling analysis of data from 499 information technology-enabled professionals showed that digital competency was significantly associated with both the DWE and workforce performance; fintech capability showed no significant relationships, whereas digital leadership was directly associated with performance. The DWE was the strongest predictor and mediated the relationship between digital competency and performance. These findings suggest that capabilities contribute to performance through their enactment in digital work systems.

title: The shifting and permeable boundaries of auditing: Evidence from early Australian examination papers
summary: This article provides insights into the shifting and permeable character of auditing and is based on analysis of 214 auditing examination papers in the archives of Certified Practising Accountants Australia for the period 1889–1952. Utilising the theoretical concept of ‘boundary-work’, we position examination papers as key discursive documents for articulating the competencies required of candidates at the time of their candidature. In contrast to conventional depictions of auditing as being mainly concerned with fraud and error detection and financial statement verification, we show that advisory work was a key theme in almost one third of all the questions studied. Interestingly, the notion of auditor independence was entirely absent from the examination regime. The analysis also shows that the emphasis on advisory work began to decline in the late-1930s as the boundary-defining knowledge and competencies associated with auditing began to narrow towards an almost exclusive focus on the audit as independent attestation.

title: Customer Relationship Management in Indian Banking: A Review of Service Quality, Digital Transformation and Customer Retention in Public and Private Sector Banks
summary: Indian banks increasingly rely on customer relationship management (CRM) systems to meet customer demand for dependable, flexible, and trustworthy digital services. This paper reviews existing CRM literature within Indian banking and focuses on public and private sector service quality, retention, and digital transformation. The paper employs a narrative style of review and organizes the literature by the following domains: conceptualization of CRM, SERVQUAL and service quality, technology driven CRM, customer satisfaction and loyalty, and public-private banking difference. CRM encompasses much more than technology; it is a holistic integration of people, processes, technologies, and the value of relationships. Relationship strength and the delivery of services are the key differentiators of public and private sector banks. Service quality is a fundamental driver of customer satisfaction. Digital transformation of banking services engenders deliberate and service quality, but also privacy, security, digital, and social concerns. The paper describes a comprehensive model of service quality, digital transformation, and the integration of sustainable CRM, trust, and of quality communication within banking systems that will satisfy and retain engaged customers. This review seeks to expand banking scholarship by situating the principles and foundations of CRM within the context of digital and sustainable banking in India.

title: Digital transformation in higher scientific education: The roles of virtual simulation, AI-assisted learning, and blended teaching
summary: The accelerating digitisation of higher education has prompted urgent questions about which technology-mediated pedagogical interventions most effectively improve student learning outcomes in scientific disciplines. Drawing on a cross-institutional survey of 1500 undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled in STEM and scientific programmes across five institution types, this study investigates the individual and joint effects of three canonical digital transformation mechanisms: virtual simulation laboratories (VSL), artificial intelligence-assisted learning (AIAAL), and blended teaching models (BTM). Employing a mixed-methods empirical framework that combines structural equation modelling (SEM), multi-level fixed-effects regression, and bootstrap mediation analysis, we estimate standardised direct effects of 0.264, 0.218, and 0.192 for VSL, AIAAL, and BTM on academic achievement, respectively. Mediation analysis reveals that self-regulated learning (SRL), collaborative knowledge construction, and cognitive engagement jointly channel 55.5% of the VSL effect and 54.7% of the AIAAL effect through indirect pathways, underscoring the primacy of process-level learning mechanisms. Moderation analysis demonstrates that institutional readiness amplifies all three technology effects by 42-68%, while disciplinary context generates the sharpest differential: VSL effects in STEM disciplines are 110% larger than in non-STEM contexts, whereas AIAAL effects remain comparably robust across disciplines. Robustness tests using instrumental variables, propensity score matching, and difference-in-differences quasi-experimental designs confirm that results are not artefacts of selection bias or omitted variable contamination. Policy scenario projections to 2030 suggest that full digital integration could reduce inter-institutional achievement gaps by 74% relative to business-as-usual. The findings contribute a theoretically grounded and empirically validated framework for evidence-based digital transformation in scientific higher education.

title: Impact of international CSR standards and associated practices on business performance in Côte d’Ivoire
summary: This study examines how international Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) standards and associated practices, including ISO certifications, energy management practices, and CO₂ emissions monitoring, are associated with the financial performance of Ivorian companies. Using data from the 2023 World Bank Enterprise Survey, we estimate regressions with sectoral and regional fixed effects and use propensity score matching as a robustness check. The results show that firms adopting green practices report higher annual sales. Energy management measures, CO₂ emissions monitoring, and internationally recognized certifications are each positively associated with sales. The study offers recommendations to support firms’ green transition.

title: MODERATING ROLE OF BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS AND AUDIT COMMITTEE MEETING FREQUENCY ON THE ESG AND FIRM VALUE RELATIONSHIP IN INDONESIA
summary: This study examines the moderating role of the Frequency of Board of Commissioners Meetings and the Frequency of Audit Committee Meetings in the relationship between ESG performance and firm value. Using 159 firm-year observations from 60 non-financial companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021–2023, we obtained data from MSCI and OSIRIS and analyzed them using moderated multiple regression. The results show that ESG performance has a positive and significant effect on firm value, consistent with agency and stakeholder theories. The Frequency of Board of Commissioners Meetings does not significantly moderate the relationship between ESG performance and firm value. In contrast, the Frequency of Audit Committee Meetings significantly moderates the relationship in the opposite direction to the hypothesized effect, weakening the positive relationship between ESG performance and firm value. These findings indicate that the relationship between ESG performance and firm value may vary with the characteristics of corporate governance oversight. The findings also highlight that meeting frequency, when considered as a quantitative governance measure, may not fully capture the substantive aspects of oversight. This study has implications for management, investors, and regulators by emphasizing the importance of considering the quality and substance of corporate governance oversight alongside meeting frequency.

title: Digital Transformation and Data-Driven Retail Execution in FMCG: An Empirical Study of HCCB’s RED/GREEN Performance Measurement Framework
summary: Retail execution in fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) depends on the ability to convert dispersed outlet-level observations into timely managerial action. This study examines how structured field data capture and performance measurement can support retail execution in the context of Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages (HCCB). The study combines an empirical retailer-survey dataset with an exploratory case-study perspective and draws on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the Resource-Based View (RBV), and Dynamic Capabilities theory. The raw dataset contains 257 submitted responses. After excluding records without both shop name and market area and deduplicating repeated outlet-area combinations, 240 unique outlet-area observations were retained. Coca-Cola assets were reported in 81.7% of these observations. Observed availability was high for Thums Up (95.8%), Coca-Cola (93.3%), Sprite (90.8%), Fanta (85.4%) and Maaza (74.2%), while lower availability was recorded for Diet Coke (17.1%), Coca-Cola 0 Sugar (15.4%), Charged (17.9%), Minute Maid (30.4%) and Rim Zim Soda (36.2%). Pepsi was reported in 36.7% of observations, Campa in 19.2%, and 41.7% reported no competition. Chi-square tests identified significant associations between asset availability and P&G outlet classification, no-competition status, and Pepsi presence; these results indicate association rather than causation. The study proposes a research-oriented RED/GREEN measurement architecture linking structured capture, execution measurement, dashboards, managerial prioritisation and verification. Machine-learning applications for outlet-risk prediction, route optimisation, demand forecasting and image-assisted compliance are proposed as future capabilities rather than documented HCCB systems. The study contributes an empirical FMCG retail-execution case while maintaining a clear boundary between observed field evidence, secondary contextual evidence and proposed analytics. Keywords: FMCG; digital transformation; retail execution; sales force automation; RED/GREEN; data-driven decision making; HCCB; outlet analytics; dynamic capabilities

title: A anatomia da disrupção digital nas organizações contemporâneas: desafios da transformação digital na gestão estratégica de operações e Supply Chain
summary: O presente artigo analisa a transformação digital como fenômeno organizacional de ordem sistêmica, com ênfase na gestão estratégica de operações e supply chain. Por meio de revisão bibliográfica e análise histórico-evolutiva, examina-se a trajetória das organizações desde o paradigma taylorista-fordista até a Indústria 4.0, identificando os vetores tecnológicos, culturais e estruturais que condicionam o êxito ou o fracasso das iniciativas de digitalização. Constata-se que, a despeito dos volumosos investimentos no setor — estimados em US$ 3,4 trilhões até 2026 (IDC, 2024) —, aproximadamente 70% dos projetos de transformação digital não alcançam seus objetivos estratégicos (MCKINSEY & COMPANY, 2023), fenômeno aqui denominado paradoxo da adoção tecnológica. O artigo propõe uma tipologia tridimensional das barreiras à transformação — cognitiva, cultural e estrutural — e discute os vetores críticos de sucesso identificados em estudos longitudinais conduzidos por instituições de referência internacional.

title: Embedded corporate social responsibility in small informal firms in Indonesia
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how corporate social responsibility (CSR) is practiced in small informal enterprises in Surabaya, Indonesia, and to show that CSR is embedded in local community norms rather than treated as a strategic or voluntary activity. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a qualitative research design based on 23 in-depth interviews with owner-managers of small informal enterprises. Findings The findings reveal that CSR practices are driven by community relationships and social obligations. These practices mainly take the form of philanthropic and service-oriented behaviors that are inseparable from economic performance and ethical conduct. Environmental sustainability is given less importance, as community norms emphasize solidarity and respect over abstract ecological concerns. The results challenge conventional CSR frameworks, such as Carroll’s pyramid, by demonstrating that economic, ethical and philanthropic responsibilities are intertwined in community-embedded small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Originality/value This study contributes to SME CSR literature by highlighting the relational and culturally embedded nature of responsibility in emerging economies, offering an alternative perspective to dominant CSR models.

title: The impact of empathetic and flexible leadership behaviors and digital transformation on marketing performance in Vietnamese female-led SMEs: The mediating role of marketing process innovation
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractIn the era of rapid digital evolution, navigating the digital paradox remains a critical challenge for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) seeking to convert technological capabilities into commercial outcomes. This study examines the relationships between empathetic and flexible leadership behaviors, digital transformation, and marketing performance through the mediating mechanism of marketing process innovation under varying levels of competitive intensity within female-led SMEs. A cross-sectional survey was administered from May to August 2025 to 265 female enterprise owners and senior executives of registered female-led SMEs in Vietnam, recruited via a structured purposive sampling design. Applying Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), the empirical findings indicate that empathetic and flexible leadership behaviors and digital transformation are significantly associated with marketing process innovation, with leadership behaviors demonstrating the strongest direct relationship (β = 0.376, p < 0.001). Furthermore, marketing process innovation partially mediates the relationship between digital transformation and marketing performance (indirect effect β = 0.103, p < 0.001; total indirect effect of the system confirms structural transmission), while competitive intensity positively moderates the relationship between marketing process innovation and marketing performance (β = 0.104, p < 0.05). Complementary fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) reveals that high marketing performance is achieved through the configurational alignment of leadership behaviors, digital maturity, and process innovation in highly competitive settings. These findings highlight the strategic value of integrating behavioral adaptability with digital initiatives to optimize marketing processes in female-led enterprises.

title: Advancing International Climate Cooperation for Small Island States: Insights from a Bibliometric Analysis of SDG 17 Implementation
summary: Under Sustainable Development Goal 17 (SDG 17) and related strategies, small island states (SISs) have gradually moved from commitment to practice in terms of international cooperation on climate change governance in an era of polycrisis; therefore, there is a need to analyze past progress, current trends, and future developments in this field. Through bibliometric analysis, this study analyzes academic trends in international cooperation for SISs with regard to climate change adaptation and mitigation. It then evaluates the main features of the selected publications from the perspective of SDG 17 implementation. The major dimensions of SDG 17 discussed in the relevant literature include capacity building, finance and trade, technology, and systemic issues. Key SDG 17 targets, such as partnership building, technology transfer, climate finance, and data capacity enhancement, are addressed in the existing research. Relatively little attention has been paid to institutional coupling mechanisms, long-term cooperation, policy autonomy, and interdisciplinary integration. Future actions should be based on the development of cooperation mechanisms, the construction of regional collaborative networks, the localization of technology, the effectiveness of long-term capacity building, and the integration of data and policies. Furthermore, it is necessary to explore sustainable and replicable models of international cooperation, and to improve the framework for mapping research to SDG 17 targets.

title: TRANSITION OF SMALL BUSINESS ENTITIES TO IFRS IN UZBEKISTAN: PRACTICAL PROBLEMS AND STRATEGIC SOLUTIONS
summary: This paper examines the practical problems associated with adapting small business entities in Uzbekistan to International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). It focuses on differences between national accounting requirements and IFRS, the need for qualified specialists and methodological support, and the role of digital technologies. The paper also considers recent reforms and proposes practical measures for gradual and effective adaptation.

title: Digital Adoption and Green Competitive Advantage: Protocol for a Bibliometric Analysis and Systematic Literature Review
summary: Tempel teks berikut pada kotak deskripsi OSF. Teks ini menjelaskan tujuan dan keluaran yang direncanakan, tanpa angka hasil pencarian karena jumlah rekaman belum diisi. This project is a protocol for a bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review of research on digital adoption and green competitive advantage (GCA). GCA is treated as a strategic position in environmental management or green innovation. Digital adoption covers technologies such as the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, big data analytics, and related Industry 4.0 tools. Existing reviews map GCA management and sustainable digital transformation separately. This project examines the two topics as one field. The purpose is to establish the state of knowledge at that intersection and to produce an intellectual roadmap for researchers and practitioners. Bibliometric analysis traces how the literature has grown, who produces it, how authors and countries collaborate, and which themes organize the debate. The systematic review then interprets those themes and sets out a future research agenda. The review does not estimate a pooled effect. Study designs and measures in this field are too varied for a meta-analysis. Documents are limited to English-language journal articles and Scopus-indexed conference papers published from 2011 through 22 October 2026. The sole database is Scopus. A record must concern organizations and must address digital adoption and GCA together. Records on only one of the two topics are outside the review. Selection is reported with the PRISMA 2020 flow. Two corpora are formed. The broader bibliometric corpus supports the maps. The narrower full-text corpus supports interpretation and the agenda. Empirical studies in the narrower corpus are appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (2018). Low scores remain visible and inform the limitations. Five questions guide the work. They ask for the annual growth of the literature; the most influential authors, journals, institutions, and countries; the intellectual map and global collaboration; the dominant thematic clusters; and the most critical future research agenda. The expected outcomes are a dated, reproducible search record; a PRISMA flow of the Scopus corpus; performance profiles of authors, sources, institutions, and countries; VOSviewer maps of author co-citation, co-authorship, and keyword clusters; a narrative reading of those clusters; and a research agenda grounded in thin themes, limitations reported by primary studies, and the quality appraisal. These products are for scholars placing new studies in the field and for managers and policymakers who need a map of how digital resources are linked to a durable green advantage.

title: Pendampingan pada UMKM di Kete Kesua tentang Fiansnial Tzeknologi
summary: MSMEs in the Kete Kesu tourism area (North Toraja) face challenges regarding limited access to capital, manual financial record-keeping, and a reliance on cash payments, all of which constrain sales potential among tourists. Financial technology (fintech) offers a strategic solution for business modernization. Implementation Method: A participatory approach with phased mentoring was employed, comprising three main stages: (1) Preparation: Needs assessment, obtaining permits, and module development. (2) Implementation: Financial literacy workshops and one-on-one technical training for activating QRIS and digital financial recording applications. (3) Evaluation: Pre- and post-test measurements, weekly transaction monitoring, and the establishment of sustainability champions. Research Results: (a) An 85% increase in the partners' understanding and digital financial literacy. (b) Successful adoption of the cashless payment system (QRIS) by dozens of local MSMEs. (c) Transition of cash recording methods from manual systems to smartphone-based digital accounting applications. (d) Enhanced operational efficiency, accountability, and sales revenue potential for merchants in the tourism area.

title: The Effect of Green Accounting and Corporate Social Responsibility Implementation on the Financial Performance of Energy Sector Companies Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange
summary: This study is urgent because understanding how green accounting and CSR affect financial performance can support sustainable business practices in energy sector companies. This study aims to analyze the impact of Green Accounting and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) implementation on the financial performance of energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2019-2024 period. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data obtained from financial statements, annual reports, and corporate sustainability reports. The study population consisted of 91 energy sector companies. Through purposive sampling, a sample of 10 companies was selected for a six-year observation period. Green Accounting was measured using a dummy variable, CSR was measured using the CSR Disclosure Index based on GRI G4 guidelines, and financial performance was measured using Return on Assets (ROA). Analysis was conducted using EViews, involving panel data model selection tests (Chow, Hausman, and Lagrange Multiplier tests) and hypothesis testing (t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination). The results indicate that Green Accounting has a positive and significant effect on financial performance, with a coefficient of 63,110.1385, a t-statistic of 2.534317, and a probability of 0.0141. CSR showed a coefficient of -6,920.1940, a t-statistic of -0.245974, and a probability of 0.8066, indicating no significant effect on financial performance. Simultaneously, Green Accounting and CSR significantly influenced financial performance, with an F-statistic of 3.213313 and a probability of 0.047743. The Adjusted R-squared value of 0.070909 indicates that the model explains 7.09% of the variation in financial performance. The findings demonstrate that, on an individual basis, Green Accounting implementation has a stronger relationship with financial performance than CSR, while the combined integration of Green Accounting and CSR shows a significant relationship with the financial performance of energy sector companies.

title: Linking Biodiversity Risk Management to Supply Chain Financing: Strategic Financing Transformation Under Physical Climate Risk
summary: ABSTRACT Using panel data on Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2011 to 2024, this study examines the association between biodiversity risk management (BRM) and trade credit provision (TCP). Our results show that BRM positively impacts corporate TCP. Heterogeneity analyses show that the positive effect is statistically significant among non‐heavily‐polluting firms, high‐tech firms, firms in more competitive markets, and firms facing less stringent environmental regulation. Digital transformation and green innovation constitute significant indirect pathways, including a sequential pathway. Aggregate and acute physical climate risks strengthen this association between BRM and TCP, while chronic physical risk has no significant moderating effect. Further analyses show that greater TCP is associated with lower supply–demand mismatch and that the BRM–TCP association is insignificant among firms exhibiting potential biodiversity‐washing behavior. Our findings highlight the financing implications of BRM for sustainable supply chains.

title: From Literacy to Legacy: Modeling the Determinants of Sustainability Financial Behavior in the Millennial Generation
summary: Purpose: This study aims to analyze how Sustainability Financial Knowledge shapes Sustainability Financial Attitude and ultimately drives Sustainability Financial Behavior among Millennials, while validating the mediating role of attitude within the Knowledge Attitude Behavior (KAB) framework. Methodology: This study employed a quantitative cross-sectional survey involving 185 Indonesian Millennials selected through non-probability purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine the relationships among Sustainability Financial Knowledge, Sustainability Financial Attitude, and Sustainability Financial Behavior, including the mediating role of attitude. Findings: The study reveals that Sustainability Financial Knowledge strongly influences Sustainability Financial Attitude with a path coefficient of 0.666, while attitude significantly drives Sustainability Financial Behavior with a coefficient of 0.639. The direct effect of knowledge on behavior is relatively weak (0.140), but its indirect effect through attitude is substantially larger (0.426). These results confirm that attitude acts as a critical mediator that strengthens the transformation of knowledge into consistent sustainable financial behavior. Research limitations/implications: This study is limited by its cross-sectional design and Millennial-specific sample, suggesting that future research should use longitudinal data and broader generational comparisons to strengthen the generalizability of the findings. Originality/value: This study offers novel empirical validation of the KAB framework in the context of sustainable finance by demonstrating the pivotal mediating role of attitude in transforming financial knowledge into sustainable financial behavior among Millennials.

title: How do different forms of environmental regulation affect high-quality economic development?
summary: Environmental regulation is increasingly important for coordinating ecological protection and economic transformation, yet its influence on high-quality economic development (HQED) may differ across regulatory forms. Drawing on institutional theory, this study examines formal and informal environmental regulation across 31 Chinese provinces from 2005 to 2022. Province and year fixed effects are employed together with nonlinear, robustness, heterogeneity, and mechanism analyses. The findings show that formal environmental regulation significantly restrains HQED, whereas informal regulation promotes it. Formal regulation displays a U-shaped effect, while informal regulation follows an inverted U-shaped pattern, with both nonlinear relationships mainly evident in eastern China. Mechanism tests further show that technological innovation and industrial agglomeration help transmit the effects of environmental regulation to HQED. These findings demonstrate that the economic consequences of environmental governance depend on regulatory form and provide evidence for designing differentiated environmental policies that support sustainable economic transformation.

title: The role of audit quality in constraining earnings management and enhancing financial transparency in the MENA region
summary: Financial transparency and earnings quality remain central concerns in emerging markets, where institutional environments and governance structures vary widely. Focusing on the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, this paper reviews how audit quality affects earnings management through a systematic analysis of 24 empirical studies published between 2011 and 2023 (Page et al., 2021). The findings reveal marked regional contrasts. In North Africa, audit quality shows uneven effectiveness, with some governance mechanisms failing to constrain manipulation, while reputable auditors and regulatory reforms strengthen reporting credibility. In the Middle East, audit quality generally limits earnings manipulation when supported by robust governance practices, yet its impact weakens in settings characterized by limited investor protection, long audit tenures, or institutional constraints. Across both subregions, the influence of audit quality remains strongly shaped by governance systems, auditor attributes, and broader institutional conditions. From a practical and regulatory perspective, the results highlight the importance of strengthening governance frameworks and enhancing audit oversight to promote greater financial transparency and reporting discipline across the region.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Financial Performance in Emerging Banking Systems: Evidence from Moroccan Banks
summary: This study examines the association between documented corporate social responsibility (CSR) recognition and accounting performance in eleven Moroccan banks during 2014–2023. Reconciliation of the original 110 bank-year records identified measurement inconsistencies and led to an unbalanced estimation sample of 108 observations, or 103 for the risk burden ratio. Profitability is measured separately by net income-based returns on assets and equity and the net banking margin. Pooled and fixed effects regressions are complemented by bank and year fixed effects, bank-clustered inference, and an exhaustive restricted wild cluster bootstrap. None of the CSR coefficients in the bank and year fixed effects models is statistically significant at the 5% level. Confidence intervals remain wide, however, and only five banks change recorded recognition status. The findings provide limited associational evidence about formal recognition, rather than a causal assessment of substantive CSR practices. Remaining accounting perimeter differences and incomplete recognition records constrain interpretation and generalization.

title: Green tourism and sustainable development in ASEAN-5: Evidence from panel data
summary: Tourism plays an important role in supporting sustainable development in ASEAN; however, its expansion can also generate environmental pressures that may undermine long-term sustainability. Green tourism offers an approach to balancing tourism development with environmental conservation and resource efficiency. This study examines the relationship between green tourism and sustainable development in five ASEAN countries—Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam—during the 2006–2021 period. Green tourism is proxied by the Environmental Performance Index (EPI), Travel and Tourism Development Index (TTDI), and Renewable Energy Consumption (REC), while Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is included as a control variable. The Sustainable Development Index (SDI) is used as the dependent variable. Using panel data regression, the Fixed Effects Model (FEM) is selected as the most appropriate estimation approach. The results indicate that EPI and TTDI have positive and statistically significant relationships with SDI, suggesting that stronger environmental performance and tourism development are associated with higher levels of sustainable development. In contrast, REC and GDP show negative and statistically significant relationships with SDI. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening environmental governance, improving sustainable tourism competitiveness, and accelerating the transition toward cleaner energy systems. The study provides empirical evidence that can support policymakers in designing integrated tourism and environmental strategies to advance sustainable development across ASEAN-5 countries.

title: Sovereign Subsea Infrastructure under Coercive State Seizure and Geopolitical Contagion: Project Dawlish Dual Physical-Legal Deterrence (DAS / ML-KEM-768 & UNCLOS/ISDS DCF Valuation), Strategic Divestment from Dual-Use Orbital Assets, and the Three-Year Platform 37 Execution Architecture
summary: 【English Abstract】 As hyperscale artificial general intelligence (AGI) and fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) transition from experimental clusters to planetary-scale critical infrastructure, passive reliance on dual-use Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations and unprotected terrestrial landing stations exposes enterprise parent entities to existential sovereign expropriation and geopolitical contagion risks. Building upon the foundational Project Dawlish subsea architecture (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23577921), this monograph formalizes the executive governance, cryptographic hardware enforcement, and corporate finance protocols required to guarantee sovereign infrastructure autonomy. First, we address the compliance and legal threat of coercive state seizure of cable landing stations (CLS) or submarine trunks under pretexts of "national security." We formulate a dual physical-legal defense scheme combining Distributed Acoustic Sensing (phi-OTDR DAS) with deterministic sub-millisecond Post-Quantum Cryptographic key zeroization (NIST FIPS 203 ML-KEM-768) via Dynamic Denial, instantaneously reducing seized optoelectronic transponders to inert, non-communicating silica ("bricked glass"), paired with automatic United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and Investor-State Dispute Settlement (ISDS) arbitration claims priced via Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) Fair Market Value (FMV). Second, we resolve the chief financial officer (CFO) capital allocation dilemma regarding passive equity holdings in militarized orbital assets (SpaceX / Starshield), proving that phased divestment constitutes Maximum Value Defense against enterprise-wide ESG impairment and regulatory contagion, while full capital reallocation into Project Dawlish and Control Barrier Function Quadratic Programming (CBF-QP) hardware interlocks secures long-term Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) optimization. title: Reconstructing Digital Sovereignty through State Resilience Legal Policy: Citizen Protection after the Cyberattack on Indonesia’s Temporary National Data Center
summary: The development of information technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) has shifted the paradigm of state resilience away from protection oriented toward territorial areas and toward the protection of a borderless digital space. This shift presents new challenges for the state in protecting its citizens, as reflected in the cyberattack on Indonesia's Temporary National Data Center (PDNS) in 2024. Although Indonesia already has various regulations concerning information technology, cybersecurity, and personal data protection, national legal policy has not yet been fully able to build an integrated framework to respond to digital threats in the AI era. This research aims to analyze the legal policy of state resilience in protecting citizens through a case study of the cyberattack on PDNS, and to reconstruct legal policy based on Digital Sovereignty as a paradigm for strengthening state resilience. This research uses the normative legal research method with statutory, conceptual, and case approaches. The results show that the national legal framework remains sectoral in nature and has not been able to comprehensively integrate cybersecurity governance, data protection, and the use of AI. Therefore, this research offers a reconstruction of legal policy based on Digital Sovereignty, which places control over data, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, and AI governance as a new foundation for strengthening state resilience while guaranteeing the protection of citizens' constitutional rights in the era of digital transformation. The proposed model integrates data sovereignty, infrastructure resilience, AI accountability, supply chain security, and digital human capacity through preventive, adaptive, rights based governance mechanisms for public institutions.

title: Service-oriented transformation breeds digital catering: variation by ownership
summary: Purpose The literature has attributed enterprise digital catering to corporate finance and corporate governance factors, including operational pressure and individual or organizational characteristics; however, the role played by enterprise strategy in this context has been overlooked. From the perspective of enterprise ownership, this study examines the heterogeneous effects of service-oriented transformation on digital catering and identifies the moderating roles played by public attention, equity incentives, and information transparency in this context. Design/methodology/approach This study employs a propensity score matching difference-in-differences method to examine how service-oriented transformation influences digital catering and explores the underlying mechanisms from the perspective of ownership. The study uses panel data obtained from Chinese listed manufacturing enterprises between 2010 and 2023. Findings The effect of service-oriented transformation on digital catering varies across different ownership structures. Service-oriented transformation stimulates digital catering among state-owned enterprises (SOEs) but has no statistically significant effect on non-SOEs. These findings indicate that SOEs have strong incentives to engage in digital catering because of their affiliation with the government administrative system. Further analysis reveals that, in the context of internal governance, both equity incentives and information transparency weaken the stimulating effect of service-oriented transformation on digital catering. In contrast, external public attention strengthens this effect. Social implications This study helps both policymakers and regulators understand the key drivers of enterprise digital catering in contexts involving policy-driven service-oriented transformation. These findings provide implications for regulating opportunistic disclosure practices and encouraging manufacturing enterprises to undertake substantive transformation. Originality/value This study addresses the gap in enterprise digital catering research related to strategic perspectives. It extends catering theory to the context of digitalization and deepens our understanding of how enterprises that exhibit different ownership structures respond differently to service-oriented transformation. The findings also provide empirical evidence to support a theoretical framework that links strategic transformation with noneconomic behavior. Additionally, this study has policy implications for efforts to implement service-oriented transformation and promote a sustainable digitalization.

title: National governance and corporate social responsibility performance in a conflict affected frontier market
summary: Abstract This paper investigates the linkage between the quality of governance at the national level and corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance in publicly traded firms in Palestine. Based on the frameworks of agency theory, stakeholder theory, and legitimacy theory, the study tests six hypotheses related to each dimension of the WGI framework by the World Bank: VC (voice and accountability), PS (political stability), GE (government effectiveness), RQ (regulatory quality), RL (rule of law), and CC (control of corruption). CSR performance is measured using corporate social responsibility expenditures, representing the real monetary investment of the firms in social and environmental operations. This study utilizes an unbalanced panel data set for 473 firm-year observations from 43 publicly traded companies on the Palestine Exchange during the period 2014–2024, using fixed-effect regression as the main approach and system GMM as the robustness test. As can be observed from the findings, voice and accountability, political stability and absence of violence, government effectiveness, and rule of law are found to positively and significantly impact CSR spending, whereas regulatory quality has a significant negative impact on CSR expenditure, supporting the theory of institutional substitution. Corruption control does not significantly impact CSR spending. The findings emphasize the importance of macro-institutional quality in influencing micro-level corporate social responsibility performance in a conflict-prone, frontier market environment. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening national governance as a foundation for promoting corporate contributions to sustainable development, particularly SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions), while reinforcing the role of the private sector in advancing the broader Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). These findings highlight the critical role of national governance in fostering corporate contributions to sustainable development, particularly by strengthening the institutional foundations of SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions) and reinforcing private-sector engagement in advancing the broader Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Transformación digital y su incidencia en el crecimiento económico de las medianas empresas del sector comercial en Machala, durante el período 2020-2025
summary: This research aimed to analyze, based on the perceptions of business representatives, how digital transformation is related to the economic growth of medium-sized companies in the commercial sector of Machala during the 2020–2025 period. A qualitative approach with a descriptive and interpretive scope was employed, and semi-structured interviews were conducted with representatives of fourteen companies from the sector under study. The inquiry addressed the tools implemented, the organizational areas perceived as most transformed, the main barriers to their adoption, and the economic benefits identified by the participants. The testimonies indicated that the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of ERP and CRM systems, e-commerce, social media, electronic invoicing, and inventory control platforms. According to the interviewees, these tools were associated with perceived improvements in sales, logistics, administration, and customer service, mainly due to error reduction, time optimization, operational control, and the expansion of commercial channels. Most participants estimated that the contribution of digitalization accounted for between 30% and 40% of revenue growth. It is concluded that the participants perceived a favorable relationship between digital transformation, productivity, competitiveness, and business sustainability; however, they identified barriers related to costs, resistance to change, and the shortage of digital skills.

title: FROM CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY TO STRATEGIC SUSTAINABILITY: THE CONTINGENT ROLE OF RESPONSIBLE LEADERSHIP
summary: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) is increasingly viewed as a strategic mechanism for integrating social and environmental considerations into organizational decision-making. However, limited research explains how CSR contributes to strategic sustainability orientation (SSO) and the leadership conditions under which this relationship is strengthened, particularly in emerging economies. Drawing on stakeholder theory and responsible leadership theory, this study examines the relationship between CSR and SSO and investigates the moderating role of responsible leadership (RL) in Pakistani manufacturing SMEs. Using a three-wave, time-lagged survey of 304 respondents, the hypothesized relationships were examined through regression-based moderation analysis. The findings reveal that CSR is positively associated with SSO, while RL significantly strengthens this relationship. Specifically, the CSR–SSO relationship is stronger under high levels of responsible leadership but becomes weak and statistically nonsignificant when responsible leadership is low. The study extends CSR and sustainability research by identifying responsible leadership as an important boundary condition that facilitates the strategic translation of CSR into sustainability-oriented organizational priorities. The findings also highlight the importance of developing responsible leadership capabilities alongside CSR initiatives, particularly in emerging-market SMEs. Keywords: Corporate social responsibility; strategic sustainability orientation; responsible leadership; manufacturing SMEs

title: Carbon price distortion and energy resource misallocation: evidence from China’s emissions trading scheme
summary: Abstract The Coase Theorem suggests that carbon markets should primarily perform two functions: price discovery and resource allocation. However, carbon price distortions may weaken both functions, raising concerns over resource misallocation and a possible “distortion superposition” effect. This study constructs a generalized cost function incorporating factor price distortions and carbon emission constraints to measure the degree of carbon price distortion. Using panel data for 30 Chinese provinces from 2000 to 2022 and a difference-in-differences approach, we examine how carbon price distortion affects energy resource misallocation in emissions trading scheme (ETS) pilot regions. The results show that energy misallocation is widespread across provinces and exhibits substantial regional heterogeneity. More importantly, the implementation of the ETS significantly aggravates energy misallocation in pilot areas, indicating that the policy, at its current stage, has not effectively directed energy resources toward high-efficiency and low-carbon sectors. Carbon price distortion further amplifies this adverse effect: the larger the deviation of carbon prices from their reasonable level, the stronger the ETS-induced deterioration in energy allocation. Mechanism analysis shows that carbon price distortion exacerbates energy misallocation mainly by constraining energy input and inhibiting green innovation. These findings provide empirical support for improving allowance allocation, refining carbon price formation, thereby contributing to the optimization of energy resource allocation and the achievement of China’s “dual-carbon” goals.

title: COMPANY SIZE, LEVERAGE, PROFITABILITY, SALES GROWTH, AND FREE CASH FLOW: THEIR EFFECT ON REAL EARNINGS MANAGEMENT AMONG CONSUMER NON-CYCLICAL FIRMS ON THE INDONESIAN STOCK EXCHANGE, 2022-2024
summary: Company size, leverage, profitability, sales growth, and free cash flow may all shape how firms manage real earnings. This study tests that relationship among consumer non-cyclical firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) between 2022 and 2024. The research follows a quantitative design and draws on secondary data from audited annual financial reports. Out of a population of 128 companies, purposive sampling yields a final sample of 74 firms and 222 firm-year observations. Real earnings management (REM) is measured using the Roychowdhury (2006) framework through three measurement proxies, namely abnormal operating cash flows, abnormal production expenditures, and abnormal discretionary spending. The empirical examination employs panel data regression facilitated by EViews 13. Findings from the Chow, Hausman, and Lagrange Multiplier tests designate the Random Effect Model as the most suitable estimation approach. The empirical evidence indicates that sales growth and free cash flow exert positive and statistically significant effects on real earnings management (REM). In contrast, firm size, leverage, and profitability exhibit no statistically significant association with REM. This pattern supports agency theory: the pressure to sustain sales performance, combined with the presence of discretionary cash, gives management greater room to act opportunistically through real activities manipulation. These results carry practical value for investors, creditors, and corporate governance mechanisms aiming to detect REM practices at an early stage.

title: APPLİCATİON OF ACCOUNTİNG INFORMATİON SYSTEMS İN AZERBAİJAN: A RESEARCH ON SMALL AND MEDİUM ENTERPRİSES
summary: The modern economic environment requires the rapid integration of digital technologies into business operations to ensure market sustainability and competitiveness. Small and medium enterprises in Azerbaijan play a pivotal role in diversification of the non-oil sector and employment generation. This study comprehensively analyzes the implementation level, structural architecture, and managerial impact of Accounting Information Systems within local small and medium enterprises. The research highlights the primary driving factors for automation, such as the digitalization of tax administration, electronic invoicing, and real-time cash register tracking systems introduced by the state authorities. Furthermore, the paper evaluates the direct effects of automated environments on financial transparency, optimization of asset structures, efficiency of working capital, and operational speed. It also addresses the critical barriers local enterprises face, including financial limitations, high software licensing costs, and a significant shortage of qualified digital accounting personnel. Ultimately, strategic recommendations are proposed to enhance the digital maturity of small firms through government subsidies, digital grants, and regional capacity-building training programs.

title: From AI Adoption to Institutional Preparedness: Governing Enterprises for AGI
summary: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) is increasingly discussed not merely as a technical frontier but as a social and institutional challenge. Drawing on current generative and agentic AI as diagnostic evidence, this paper examines enterprise institutional preparedness for increasingly general and autonomous AI systems through three interrelated dimensions: organizational resilience, employee protection, and social responsibility. Using conceptual and normative analysis, the paper synthesizes AI governance, organizational resilience, labor studies, corporate social responsibility, and policy frameworks to develop a forward-looking governance architecture. The framework links three levels of institutional exposure: continuity of organizational functions, preservation of worker agency, and external social legitimacy. It identifies seven preparedness components: strategic foresight, governance architecture, risk and impact assessment, human oversight, employee protection, social responsibility, and continuous learning. The analysis further distinguishes scalable risks already visible in current AI from potentially discontinuous risks associated with greater autonomy and cross-domain integration. The study shifts the unit of analysis from tool-level AI risk management to enterprise-level institutional capacity to preserve organizational continuity, worker agency, and external social legitimacy.

title: Policy Brief: Brazil's open ecosystems—Carbon stocks overlooked by climate finance
summary: Societal Impact Statement The equitable recognition of the world's open ecosystems is critical for climate justice and societal well‐being. These ecosystems provide essential services, like carbon storage, water security, and biodiversity protection, that strengthen resilience to climate change. Yet, they remain overlooked in climate finance and policy frameworks that privilege forests. By highlighting their contributions and advocating for their inclusion in international mechanisms, this Policy Brief supports more balanced environmental governance. Its recommendations aim to guide policymakers, civil society, and legislators toward strategies that ensure climate security and equitable resource distribution for present and future generations.

title: ROLES OF ACCOUNTING EDUCATION IN PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT IN THE DIGITAL ERA
summary: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has transformed economic activities, business operations, financial reporting, and professional accounting practices, creating new accounting education demands. This study examines the role of accounting education in promoting sustainable economic development in the digital era. This paper is anchored on a conceptual review of relevant literature on accounting education, digital transformation, sustainability, financial literacy, innovation, and economic development. Accounting education plays a critical role in developing digitally competent accounting professionals who can effectively apply emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud accounting, big data analytics, block-chain, and digital financial systems. Beyond technical accounting knowledge, contemporary accounting education promotes ethical decision-making, transparency, accountability, entrepreneurship, financial inclusion, and responsible resource management, all of which are essential for sustainable economic development. The paper further highlights the importance of integrating digital skills, sustainability accounting, data analytics, information technology, and professional ethics into accounting curricula to prepare learners for the changing demands of the labor market and the digital economy. The study concludes that strengthening accounting education through curriculum modernization, technological integration, industry–academia collaboration, continuous professional development, and competency-based learning can enhance productivity, employability, innovation, and responsible economic decision-making. This paper recommends that educational institutions, policymakers, professional accounting bodies, and other stakeholders should strategically reposition accounting education to respond to digital transformation and contribute meaningfully to inclusive and sustainable economic development

title: Silent Strategies: CEO Populism, Supply Chain Opacity, and Biodiversity Disclosure
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether CEO populist rhetoric is associated with corporate biodiversity disclosure and whether supply‐chain opacity conditions this relationship. Using an unbalanced panel of 1828 nonfinancial listed firms from 12 European countries over 2014–2022, the analysis comprises 15,842 firm‐year observations in the baseline estimation. Firm fixed effects, two‐stage least squares, and two‐step system GMM models are used to account for unobserved heterogeneity, potential endogeneity, and dynamic persistence. The findings show that CEO populist rhetoric is negatively associated with biodiversity disclosure and positively associated with supply‐chain opacity, indicating that stronger populist rhetoric coincides with less visible, specific, and verifiable publicly reported upstream supply‐chain information. The moderation analysis provides qualified evidence that lagged supply‐chain opacity strengthens the negative association between CEO populism and biodiversity disclosure, suggesting that executive rhetoric is more strongly related to lower nature‐related transparency when upstream information is less visible and verifiable. These findings extend the understanding of biodiversity disclosure beyond a predominantly technical reporting perspective by showing that nature‐related transparency is associated with both executive rhetorical framing and the informational conditions surrounding upstream supply chains. Integrating upper echelons theory with stakeholder and institutional perspectives, the study explains how CEO rhetoric may shape the interpretation of external accountability demands while supply‐chain opacity affects the informational conditions under which such interpretations are reflected in disclosure. The study contributes to research on executive communication, sustainability governance, biodiversity reporting, and the credibility of corporate environmental disclosure.

title: Machine Learning Meets Blockchain: A Domain-Oriented Review of Integration Mechanisms, Applications, and Open Challenges
summary: Blockchain and machine learning (ML) are combined in systems that must learn from multi-party data and keep a verifiable record of what was used and decided. This scoping-style review of a ranked sample covers seven domains: healthcare, finance, supply chain, energy, smart contracts, transportation and education. We searched Scopus and IEEE Xplore on 15 October 2026, ranked 5,195 candidate records, read 345 abstracts in rank order, coded a core corpus of 192 studies and read 38 in full. Federated learning is the most common method (93 of 192 core studies name it), and detection of fraud, intrusions and vulnerabilities is the most common task among the 38. None of the 38 reports a deployment, 24 report a measured ledger figure and two measure ledger energy. Ten use more than one privacy mechanism, and only two report accuracy with and without it. Attack tests are small, and one study tests a Sybil attacker. Studies differ too much to compare, so we do not rank domains. A ledger shows that a record has not changed, not that it was correct when written. The main gaps are realistic evaluation, shared benchmarks and reporting standards, and tested explanations for decisions made inside contracts.

title: Grassroots Environmental Discourse and the National Project “Ecological Well-Being”: Topic Modeling of Russian VKontakte Communities
summary: Effective environmental governance increasingly depends on aligning top-down policy priorities with grassroots civic practices. This study assesses the potential for integrating grassroots environmental initiatives into Russia’s National Project “Ecological Well-Being” by comparing the thematic structure of VKontakte environmental communities with six federal project areas. A corpus of 64,364 posts obtained in 2025 by 201 long-running environmental communities was collected and balanced to 30,500 texts. BERTopic, using multilingual sentence embeddings, UMAP, and HDBSCAN, assigned 15,066 posts (49.4% of the balanced corpus) to 397 stable thematic clusters, while the remaining 15,434 posts were treated as noise and excluded from the thematic comparison. Topic labels and correspondence with the National Project initiatives were subsequently assessed with DeepSeek Chat. Gap Analysis showed that 64 of the 397 topics (16.12%), comprising 3081 of the 15,066 clustered posts (20.45%), directly overlapped with at least one initiative of the National Project. The remaining 333 topics (83.88%), comprising 11,985 clustered posts (79.55%), formed a Grassroots Surplus outside the formal policy agenda. The largest overlap in terms of both topics and posts concerned biodiversity (12.34% of topics; 15.46% of posts) and the circular economy (4.79%; 5.27%, respectively), while the clean air initiative had the lowest representation (0.25%; 0.14%). Animal welfare, school and family environmental initiatives, and local recreation emerged as gateway topics that may connect everyday civic practices with national environmental programs.

title: Unveiling the Path of Sustainability Reporting Quality Through Board Governance Mechanisms: Evidence From Sub‐Saharan Africa
summary: ABSTRACT The study examines how board governance mechanisms influence the quality of sustainability reporting among listed firms in Sub‐Saharan Africa, where weak institutional frameworks increase the need for strong corporate oversight. The research employed a sample of 1530 firm‐year observations from 2015 to 2024, and applied panel fixed effects and Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) in system models to estimate the results. The findings reveal that board attributes plays a key role in shaping the quality of sustainability disclosures across the models. The novelty of this study lies in its emphasis on board governance supporting environmental sustainability over social and economic dimensions. Firms with more independent board members, higher female representation, and directors with financial, auditing, and sustainability expertise produce more credible sustainability reports. These board attributes strengthen oversight and enhance transparency and accountability. However, board size has a negative effect, suggesting that large boards may face coordination and monitoring challenges. This study contributes new evidence by extending sustainability reporting literature in Sub‐Saharan Africa, a region that remains unexplored. The results offer practical insights for firms and policymakers. Companies are encouraged to maintain a sizable board of directors that would strengthen board composition through diversity and relevant expertise. Improving external assurance of sustainability reports is also important for building trust and accountability.
