title: Analisis Kesesuaian Laporan Keuangan UMKM Dee Rumah Cake & Catering dengan SAK ETAP
summary: This study aims to analyze the extent to which the financial statements of the MSME "Dee Rumah Cake & Catering" align with the Financial Accounting Standards for Entities without Public Accountability (SAK ETAP). The study is motivated by the fact that many MSME operators have yet to implement formal financial reporting systems that meet established standards; consequently, the financial information produced lacks the full relevance and reliability required to support decision-making or facilitate access to financing. A qualitative descriptive approach, utilizing a case study method, was employed. The data analyzed include the financial statements of Dee Rumah Cake & Catering—comprising the income statement, statement of changes in equity, balance sheet, and statement of cash flows—along with other relevant supporting data. Data were collected through documentation and a literature review, while the analysis involved comparing the components, recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure of the financial statements against the provisions of SAK ETAP. The findings indicate that the financial statements of Dee Rumah Cake & Catering are not yet fully compliant with SAK ETAP. This non-compliance stems from incomplete financial statement components—specifically the absence of Notes to the Financial Statements (CaLK)—inconsistent recording and disclosure of fixed assets, misclassification of transactions within the statement of cash flows, and a lack of sufficient supporting documentation for transactions. As a result, the current financial statements remain overly simplistic and fail to fully satisfy the presentation principles mandated by SAK ETAP. This study is intended to provide recommendations for the MSME owner to enhance their understanding of accounting and implement SAK ETAP more comprehensively, thereby ensuring that financial statements become more informative and serve as a more effective basis for decision-making.

title: Evaluating Social Innovation Program through the Social Return on Investment (SROI) Method: A Case Study of the KIJANGKU Program at PT TMMIN Karawang Plant 1-2
summary: The shift of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) from a voluntary commitment to a business strategy and regulatory obligation has increased the need for measurable assessments of the social and environmental impacts of corporate sustainability initiatives. This study evaluates the effectiveness and the social, economic, and environmental value created by the KIJANGKU (Konservasi Hijau Selamatkan Lingkunganku) Social Innovation Program, implemented by PT Toyota Motor Manufacturing Indonesia (TMMIN) at Karawang Plants 1–2 during 2023–2025. Using the Social Return on Investment (SROI) approach, the study assesses the value generated relative to the program’s social investment. A total investment of IDR 381,000,000 (present value: IDR 399,237,600) produced benefits with a present value of IDR 524,762,076, yielding an SROI ratio of 1.31. Each IDR 1 invested thus generated approximately IDR 1.31 in social, economic, and environmental value. The findings indicate that KIJANGKU benefited local communities while supporting environmental conservation and sustainability. The study highlights the applicability of SROI for evaluating the broader impacts of corporate social innovation programs and their contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals).

title: CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY AS A TOOL FOR DEVELOPING A COMPANY’S CORPORATE CULTURE IN THE CONTEXT OF FOREIGN ECONOMIC ACTIVITY
summary: This article examines corporate social responsibility as a tool for developing a company’s corporate culture in the context of foreign economic activity and justifies the mechanism for integrating socially responsible practices into the management system. It summarizes scientific approaches to the interpretation of corporate social responsibility and corporate culture and identifies the areas of their interconnection with employees, partners, consumers, and stakeholders. It has been established that CSR encompasses the fulfillment of legislative and contractual obligations, the formation of corporate values, responsible employee behavior, and responsible partnerships. The areas of CSR have been systematized: responsibility toward employees, partners, and consumers; legal, financial, and reputational responsibility; and responsible resource management. This paper substantiates a mechanism for implementing CSR as a tool for developing a company’s corporate culture in the context of foreign economic activity. The mechanism is aimed at fostering shared corporate values, adapting to the requirements of international stakeholders, and integrating socially responsible approaches into foreign economic activity. A system of indicators has been proposed to evaluate the effectiveness of the mechanism in the areas of CSR implementation, corporate culture development, human resources, partnerships, reputation, and foreign economic activity. The system includes the level of implementation of CSR measures, the extent to which business processes are guided by the principles of social responsibility, employee satisfaction with working conditions, the proportion of staff participating in training, the level of fulfillment of contractual obligations, and the number of repeat and international contracts. The study identifies the following vectors of corporate culture development: internal, managerial, reputational, partnership-based, consumer-oriented, and foreign economic. The practical significance of these findings lies in the ability of enterprises engaged in foreign economic activity to apply this mechanism to develop corporate culture, strengthen their business reputation, and enhance the reliability of their partnerships.

title: The Effect of Profitability, Audit Opinion, Firm Size, and Leverage on the Timeliness of Financial Reporting in Manufacturing Companies Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2022–2024 Period
summary: Timely financial reporting provides relevant information for economic decision-making, yet reporting delays remain a concern in capital markets. This study examines the associations of profitability, audit opinion, firm size, and leverage with financial reporting timeliness among manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2022–2024. A quantitative approach used secondary data comprising 303 firm-year observations, analyzed through logistic regression in SPSS. Profitability and audit opinion exhibited statistically significant associations with reporting timeliness, whereas firm size and leverage did not show significant associations within the sample. These findings identify financial performance and audit opinion as relevant correlates of timely reporting in the companies examined. The study contributes empirical evidence on financial reporting timeliness in Indonesia’s manufacturing sector and offers practical implications for corporate managers monitoring financial performance and audit processes, as well as investors evaluating corporate reporting practices. The results also provide a basis for further research on the determinants of timely financial reporting.

title: Pengaruh Auditor Size, Audit Tenure, Audit Specialization, Firm Size dan Leverage Terhadap Earning Quality (Pada Perusahaan Perbankan Yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) Tahun 2021-2025)
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of Auditor Size, Audit Tenure, Audit Specialization, Firm Size, and Leverage on Earnings Quality in banking companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) in 2021–2025. The research method used in this study is a quantitative method. The data used are secondary data obtained from the official financial statements and annual reports of the sampled companies through the official IDX website. Data processing and analysis were conducted using SPSS software. The results of this study indicate that, partially, Auditor Size, Audit Tenure, and Audit Specialization have a positive and significant effect on Earnings Quality. Firm Size has a negative effect on Earnings Quality, indicating that the larger the company, the more complex its operational activities, which may increase the risk of earnings management practices. Meanwhile, Leverage has no effect on Earnings Quality, indicating that earnings quality is not solely determined by the company's financing structure but is also influenced by other factors, such as audit quality, corporate governance, and internal control.

title: Methods for evaluating efficiency in development cooperation
summary: Development policy is under pressure. Shrinking resources are confronted with growing challenges. This further increases the importance of the efficient use of development funds. Evaluations are used for examining the efficiency of development interventions and for making recommendations to enhance their success. However, assessing efficiency is among the more demanding tasks in evaluation. The aim in this discussion paper is to support the evaluation of efficiency. To this end, the paper considers different understandings of efficiency – as an evaluation criterion, in the context of auditing and in welfare and health economics – and presents a methods catalogue for evaluating the efficiency of development projects and programmes, structured along various features. The methods catalogue is structured according to the purpose or interest of evaluations: methods designed to compare the efficiency of different interventions and methods designed to evaluate efficiency improvement potentials within a single intervention. Overall, the catalogue comprises 13 methods or groups of methods, including well-established methods, such as cost-benefit analysis, cost-effectiveness analysis and benchmarking of unit costs, as well as less established methods, such as social return on investment, systematic screening approaches and structured expert judgement. To meet the growing demands on evaluating efficiency, we call on commissioners and evaluators to make use of the full breadth of methods outlined in the catalogue. The discussion paper brings together the necessary action-oriented foundations for this purpose by providing guidance on the selection of methods and reflecting on their strengths and limitations. Through the informed and targeted application of methods, the efficiency and utility of evaluation can be enhanced.

title: Sustainably-Lean Architecture (SLA): An Integrated Framework for Spatial Stewardship, Lifecycle Optimization, and Sustainable Infrastructure Development
summary: This paper presents the Sustainably-Lean Architecture (SLA) Framework - a new conceptual framework developed to support better decision-making in the built environment by adopting an integrated perspective based on principles of sustainability, lean construction, lifecycle asset management, digital transformation, and spatial stewardship. This framework responds to ongoing problems within current practices of infrastructure and building development that include inefficient use of resources, unused spaces, high lifecycle costs, growing demands on affordability, negative impacts on the environment, as well as disjointed decision-making. The proposed framework emphasizes the importance of the long-term value of built assets through evidence-driven planning, continual improvement, lifecycle perspective, and responsible use of resources. title: A strategic approach to addressing climate change’s impact on business, highlighting the role of corporate social responsibility
summary: This study aims to address issues associated with climate change and environmental impacts on businesses from a strategic perspective and extensively highlighting the role of corporate social responsibility (CSR), while emphasizing and introducing the context of investment risks and the essence of shielding against risks and the crucial need for mitigating measures. Furthermore, the stakeholder perspective has been extended into shared value creation and translating to equity in the context of the resource-based view. The quantitative method was applied based on inferential statistics, supplemented with interviews. Structured and semi-structured questionnaires and interview materials were applied in data collection from randomly drawn participants and respondents from the population. The population sampled consists of up to 408 responses captured in Roma. The relationship between investment risks and brand reputation and also with brand equity in each case from multiple regression showed statistical significance at the 5% level of significance, as the p -value in each case is less than 0.05 (< 0.05). The results of these studies also confirm that CSR has a positive and significant relationship with trust, which also aligns with the assumption of this study on the composite relationship existing and connecting the two groups on their perceptions of investment risks based on resource conservation against state activism and the perception of litigation being redressed. The results indicate that organizations can gain a competitive advantage through shared value from a strategic point of view. Thus, it is imperative for businesses to adopt strategic measures, such as creating and building shields or hedge against investment risks, and fuse CSR into their business models and brands to address emerging issues as highlighted following the present dynamics and prevailing trends.

title: Does the rural digital economy enhance green total factor productivity of agriculture? An empirical approach using double machine learning
summary: Introduction In the context of the green transformation of agriculture, the digital economy offers a novel pathway to mitigate environmental externalities and operational inefficiencies. Recognizing that agricultural digitalisation relies heavily on the spillover of macro-level digital resources, this study constructs a multidimensional rural digital economy (RDE) framework. Methods Employing a double machine learning (DML) model on a panel dataset of 30 Chinese provinces from 2011 to 2022, we empirically investigate the impact of the RDE on agricultural green total factor productivity (GTFP). Results We find that: (1) The RDE exerts a positive effect on GTFP. Dimensional analysis strictly confirms that digital industry development and industrial digital transformation have positive linkages with this productivity growth, whereas basic infrastructure alone is insufficient. (2) Mechanism analyses demonstrate that the RDE empowers green agriculture by optimizing inter-sectoral factor allocation and significantly reducing agricultural polluting energy intensity; however, the mediating role of government digital policy attention is not statistically established. (3) To accurately capture asymmetric effects, group-based heterogeneity tests reveal that the empowerment effect of the RDE is significantly stronger in provinces with larger cultivated scales. Discussion These findings indicate that the RDE currently empowers green agriculture primarily through structural factor reallocation and precision energy management rather than immediate technological leaps. To overcome hardware-software structural lags and mitigate scale disadvantages faced by smallholders, policymakers should pivot toward enhancing farmers’ digital literacy, expanding shared digital socialized services, and implementing market-based environmental governance.

title: Ecological Belonging and the Economics of Climate Change
summary: Climate change reveals a fundamental mismatch between humanity’s material and biological dependence on a shared ecological system and the institutional arrangements governing economic production, consumption, investment, and political responsibility. This article develops an interpretation of climate change through the Philosophy of Belonging and its mature Ethics of Belonging. It argues that the climate crisis is not merely a problem of negative externalities, insufficient carbon pricing, or international coordination. It also reflects a failure of institutional correspondence and potentially inadequate collective adaptability. The analysis is organized around four scientifically informed and revisable ontological principles: constitutive integration, imperfect belonging, stratified reality, and the synchronic and diachronic dimensions of existence. These principles explain how economic and institutional systems can generate present prosperity while undermining the ecological conditions necessary for future human development. The article extends the Ethics of Belonging to environmental governance through three interrelated conditions of adequate social ethics: developing the belonging needs of constituent individuals and groups, enabling effective initiative and participation, and orienting collective decisions toward the development of the broader community. Together, these conditions provide a framework for investigating the relationship between social inclusion, institutional learning, and collective adaptability. Individual ethics is incorporated through six interacting psychological developmental steps, connecting embodied experience, instincts, emotional development, love, social significance, existential meaning, conscious presence, and mentalization to the possibility of reflective ecological agency. The framework is examined in dialogue with environmental externality theory, integrated assessment models, ecological economics, polycentric governance, environmental justice, and the capability approach. The article proposes an institutional architecture combining credible ecological constraints, carbon pricing, public investment, social protection, participatory governance, international cooperation, and institutional adaptability. Nine testable propositions identify potential relationships among climate policy, social participation, economic transformation, emissions reduction, and long-term adaptive capacity. The central contribution is to reinterpret ecological sustainability as a problem of organized belonging: effective responses to climate change depend not only on technological and economic instruments but also on the development of the individuals, groups, and institutions through which societies acquire the capacity to learn, coordinate, and transform. The article offers a conceptual and empirical research program rather than a new quantitative estimate of climate damages or a claim that social inclusion alone can resolve the climate crisis.

title: A Purpose-Based Theory of Corporate Law
summary: Modern corporate law scholarship focuses on flexible, dynamic questions: should multiple-class shares be permitted? To what extent should staggered boards be implemented? Even when making the more structural inquiry—what is a corporation, and what is its purpose?—corporate jurists tend toward generalizations: perceiving corporate law as either contract law, property law, or public law, and being either shareholderists (“shareholder primacy” advocates) or stakeholderists (“corporate social responsibility” advocates). In these accounts, fiduciary duties presumably run directly to shareholders or stakeholders. However, as this Article demonstrates, careful examination of corporate law (in Delaware and many other jurisdictions) reveals that all of these prevailing conceptions are, positively and normatively, inaccurate. This Article offers a new paradigm through which to examine corporate law. It provides an integrative theory, fully congruent with both existing law and policy analysis, showing that corporate law is not any other field, but has its own structure, with uniquely beneficial economic and practical implications. At the heart of corporate law’s anatomy is a simple, yet profound, fact: the corporation is a person with a purpose. The corporation itself has Hohfeldian relationships with its stakeholders, shareholders, and fiduciaries. The benefit of both stakeholders and shareholders is derived from the degree to which the corporation attains its purpose (for example, the lawful pursuit of profit). Directors and other fiduciaries, in turn, have an obligation to cause the corporation to achieve its purpose. While corporate purpose, personhood, stakeholders, shareholders, and fiduciaries are all subjects of heated discussion, this Article is the first to tie them together, providing a fully self-explanatory picture of their mutual interactions. Doing away with both the “contract/property” and “shareholder/stakeholder” dichotomies, this Article applies the theory to several high-currency topics, including shareholder activism, corporations’ constitutional rights, the rise of LLCs and other “alternative” corporations, mandatory arbitration, and Senator Warren’s Accountable Capitalism Act. At each turn, the purpose-based theory of corporate law produces more refined conclusions, and charts a way forward—from conceptions devised in the 1980s, to a nuanced framework, capable of providing better answers to the many issues corporate law faces in its current state of flux.

title: Fintech-Driven Transformation of Financial Markets and Investment Decision-Making: A Conceptual Study
summary: Financial technology (fintech) is changing how financial markets operate and how investors access, interpret, and act on financial information. Digital payments, mobile investment platforms, robo-advisory services, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, big-data analytics, blockchain, and automated trading have altered the speed, reach, and informational basis of financial decisions. Yet the consequences are not uniformly beneficial: greater access and analytical capacity can coexist with cyber risk, algorithmic opacity, behavioural overconfidence, platform dependence, and unequal digital capabilities. This conceptual study synthesizes the literature review supplied for the paper, which covers fintech adoption, digital transformation in financial services, capital-market infrastructure, AI-supported investment decisions, financial risk management, mutual-fund choice, and the behavioural implications of personal-finance applications. The study proposes an integrated conceptual model linking fintech capabilities to investment decision-making quality through information accessibility, analytical support, transaction efficiency, and trust. Behavioural biases act as mediators, while financial literacy, digital capability, and governance quality moderate the proposed relationships. Expected outcomes include decision quality, portfolio alignment, participation, and market efficiency, subject to risks and institutional conditions. The model is conceptual and is not presented as empirically validated. It offers propositions for future testing and practical implications for investors, fintech providers, financial institutions, and regulators. The central argument is that fintech creates value when technological capability is combined with informed users, transparent design, robust safeguards, and meaningful human oversight.

title: A Competency Framework for Governance: Integrating Individual and Team-Level Capabilities
summary: Introduction: In today's organizations, governance has transformed into a multi-layered structure that is not limited to corporate oversight and compliance processes, but is also related to stakeholder management, digitalization, ethical responsibility, transparency, and team-based decision-making processes. This transformation necessitates a reevaluation of the competencies that individuals and teams involved in governance processes must possess—a brief contextualization of the problem addressed by the article that is presented to the reader; ii) objective: The aim of this study is to develop an integrated conceptual framework that explains the relationship between individual and collective competencies, organizational governance capacity, and governance mechanisms at the team level. iii) methodology: The study is a conceptual and theoretical literature review. Competency modeling, corporate governance, digital governance, stakeholder management, and team-level governance literature have been examined; classical competency theories have been integrated with contemporary studies to propose a comprehensive model. iv) Results: The review shows that effective governance is not only dependent on structural mechanisms but also on competencies such as leadership, ethical judgment, communication, data-driven decision-making, stakeholder sensitivity, and intra-team coordination. v) conclusions: The study reveals that governance competencies should be considered dynamic capabilities that support accountability at the individual, collective, and team levels, and proposes a behavior-based governance competency framework for contemporary organization

title: Regularized Government Accounting Supervision and Suppliers’ Cash Holdings: Evidence from Supply Chain Spillover Effects
summary: This article takes the reform pilot of strengthening accounting supervision carried out by the Ministry of Finance in selected provinces and municipalities at the end of 2020 as a quasi‑natural experiment, and adopts the difference‑in‑differences method to investigate the supply chain spillover effect of regularized government accounting supervision on the cash holding level of supplier firms. The study finds that when midstream firms are located in regions with the accounting supervision reform pilot, the cash holding level of their supplier firms decreases significantly. Mechanism tests show that regularized government accounting supervision functions mainly through two channels, namely reducing supply chain risks faced by suppliers and increasing the supply of trade credit. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the above effect is more pronounced among supplier firms that are state‑owned enterprises, have high customer concentration, and belong to high‑tech industries. This research expands the research boundary of the economic consequences of government accounting supervision, reveals the microeconomic effects of external regulatory institutions transmitted through supply chain relationships, and provides empirical evidence for improving China’s accounting supervision system and enhancing the financial resilience of supply chains.

title: Data-driven culture and sustainable performance: the mediating role of supply chain integration
summary: Digital transformation has increased the availability of data in operations and supply chain management, yet many organisations struggle to translate data into improved operational and sustainability outcomes. Drawing on the resource-based view, this study examines how a data-driven culture (DDC) influences supply chain integration and sustainable performance. Survey data were collected from 242 managers in large industrial firms in Jordan and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The results show that DDC significantly enhances both internal and external supply chain integration. Furthermore, external integration with suppliers and customers positively influences sustainable performance, while internal integration does not show a significant direct effect. These findings highlight the importance of combining data-driven decision-making with collaborative supply chain relationships to improve operational coordination, resource efficiency, and sustainability performance.

title: Digital Transformation of Accounting in MSMEs in Timor-Leste: The Role of Accounting Technology Adoption and Organizational Readiness in Improving Financial Management Effectiveness
summary: Digital transformation has created opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to improve financial management through accounting technology. However, adopting digital technology alone may not ensure effective financial management without adequate organizational readiness. Previous studies have examined digital technology adoption and organizational factors separately, leaving room for an integrated conceptual framework, particularly in the context of SMEs in Timor-Leste. This study aims to develop a conceptual model explaining the role of accounting technology adoption and organizational readiness in supporting financial management effectiveness. A conceptual research design was employed through an integrative literature review of relevant scholarly publications on digital transformation, accounting technology adoption, organizational readiness, and SME financial management. The literature synthesis informed the development of a model that positions accounting technology adoption and organizational readiness as two independent constructs associated with financial management effectiveness. The proposed model highlights the importance of integrating digital accounting solutions with organizational resources, competencies, management support, and commitment. The novelty lies in combining the technological and organizational dimensions within a single conceptual framework tailored to the context of SMEs in Timor-Leste. The model provides a foundation for future empirical testing and offers practical insights for developing context-sensitive digital accounting strategies to strengthen SME financial management.

title: THE ESSENCE, NECESSITY, AND SIGNIFICANCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN THE BANKING SYSTEM
summary: This article examines the essence, necessity, significance, and types of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, highlighting their role as key drivers of innovation in the banking system. Particular attention is given to the potential of AI technologies to optimize credit scoring processes, enhance the speed and quality of customer service, and facilitate the early detection of fraudulent activities. Furthermore, the article provides a theoretical overview of the positive contributions of artificial intelligence to banks' operational efficiency and financial stability in the context of rapid digital transformation. The study also analyzes the practical applications of AI technologies in the banking and financial sectors at both international and national levels, emphasizing their growing importance in improving banking operations and supporting the development of innovative financial services.

title: Towards the protection of shareholders' proposal rights in limited liability companies—From the perspective of the validity of shareholders' meeting resolution
summary: Though not explicitly established under the current Company Law, the shareholder proposal right constitutes a core entitlement for minority shareholders of limited liability companies to engage in corporate governance, and its potential exercise would directly bear on the validity of shareholders' meeting resolutions. Focusing on limited liability companies as the research subject, this paper integrates their characteristics of personal nexus and closedness to sort out the fundamental theories concerning the shareholder proposal right and the validity of shareholders' meeting resolutions. It further dissects procedural obstacles that would be encountered in the potential exercise of the shareholder proposal right, such as shareholding percentage thresholds and deficiencies in relief mechanisms, as well as the ensuing disputes over the validity of resolutions. In response to issues in judicial practice, including inconsistent criteria for identifying defects in the proposal right and ambiguous rules regarding the types of resolution validity, this paper puts forward paths for institutional construction of the shareholder proposal right from three dimensions: clarifying the rules governing the exercise of the proposal right, establishing standards for determining resolution validity, and designing judicial relief and dispute resolution mechanisms. This study provides theoretical reference and guidance for legislative supplementation and judicial rule-making concerning internal governance of limited liability companies.

title: Analysis of the Influence of Ownership Structure and Capital Structure on the Performance of Investment Product Companies Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of ownership structure and capital structure on firm performance in the investment product sector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2021–2024 period. Ownership structure is proxied by institutional ownership and managerial ownership, while capital structure is measured using the Debt to Equity Ratio (DER). Firm performance is represented by Price to Book Value (PBV) as a market-based performance indicator that reflects investors' perceptions of a firm's value and future prospects. This research employs a quantitative approach using panel data obtained from annual financial statements and market data. The research sample consists of 11 holding and investment companies with a total of 44 observations over the study period. Panel data regression analysis is applied using the Fixed Effect Model (FEM), which is selected based on the results of model selection tests. Classical assumption tests and hypothesis testing are conducted to ensure the validity and reliability of the regression model. The results indicate that institutional ownership, managerial ownership, and capital structure simultaneously affect firm performance. Partially, institutional ownership and managerial ownership have a positive and significant effect on PBV, suggesting that ownership-based governance mechanisms enhance monitoring effectiveness and improve firm performance and market valuation. In contrast, capital structure, as measured by DER, does not have a significant effect on firm performance. These findings imply that, in the holding and investment sector, firm performance is more strongly influenced by governance quality and investment decision effectiveness than by leverage levels. This study is expected to contribute empirical evidence to corporate governance literature and provide practical insights for managers and investors in financial decision-making.

title: Pendampingan Tata Kelola Digital ‘Aisyiyah melalui Penguatan Manajemen dan Sinergi Lokal–Global
summary: The rapid advancement of digital technology requires community organizations to strengthen governance systems that are effective, transparent, and adaptive. This community service program aimed to enhance the digital governance capacity of ‘Aisyiyah through collaboration among Universitas Muhammadiyah Jambi, the Regional Leadership of ‘Aisyiyah Jambi, and the Special Branch Leadership of ‘Aisyiyah New South Wales, Australia. The program employed socialization, training, mentoring, and evaluation methods to support the implementation of digital-based organizational administration, communication, documentation, and website-based information management. The results demonstrated significant improvements in participants’ knowledge and skills in utilizing digital technologies to improve organizational governance. Furthermore, the collaboration between local and international partners facilitated the exchange of best practices and strengthened the sustainability of organizational digital transformation. This program provides a practical model for assisting community organizations in achieving modern, professional, and sustainable digital governance.

title: Efektivitas Implementasi Transformasi Digital Rekam Medis Elektronik
summary: Electronic medical record (EMR) implementation in regional hospitals still faces technological, human resource, and governance challenges, while HOT-Fit-based studies in regional hospitals remain limited. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of EMR digital transformation, its supporting and inhibiting factors, and its impact on service effectiveness at Arosuka Regional Hospital, Solok Regency. A qualitative case study approach was used. Five informants were selected purposively through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation, analyzed thematically using NVivo 15 within the HOT-Fit framework. The results show that 20 of 24 service units (83.33%) actively use the EMR, with easier recording, information access, and service efficiency. Waiting times improved to under 60 minutes. However, user competence is uneven, training is not routine, usage across units is inconsistent, and network disruptions persist. It is concluded that EMR implementation is fairly effective but not yet optimal, and Net Benefit will be maximized when the Human, Organization, and Technology dimensions are aligned.

title: THE EFFECT OF SUPPLY CHAIN AGILITY ON BUSINESS CONTINUITY OF FREIGHT FORWARDING COMPANIES UNDER GLOBAL SUPPLY CHAIN DISRUPTIONS
summary: Purpose - This study aims to analyze the influence of supply chain agility on business continuity in freight forwarding companies in dealing with uncertainty and supply chain disruption. Design/methodology/approach - The study used a quantitative, explanatory design. The study collected data through questionnaires from 55 freight forwarding companies and analyzed them using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings - The results show that supply chain agility has a positive, significant effect on business continuity, with a path coefficient of 0.953, a t-statistic of 35.171, and a p-value < 0.001. An R² value of 0.909 indicates that supply chain agility can explain 90.9% of business continuity variations. These findings confirm the importance of responsiveness to change, operational flexibility, resource reconfiguration, and information utilization in maintaining business continuity in freight forwarding companies. Originality/value - This research contributes by positioning business continuity as a direct outcome of supply chain agility in freight forwarding companies. This study expands the application of dynamic capabilities theory in the logistics services sector by showing that agility serves as a strategic capability for maintaining business functions during supply chain disruptions.

title: PENGEMBANGAN MODEL TRANSFORMASI DIGITAL MANAJEMEN SUMBER DAYA MANUSIA BERBASIS KARAKTER KEJUJURAN
summary: This study aims to formulate a conceptual model of digital transformation in human resource management (HRM) that places honesty as a fundamental principle in managing tasks, reporting, communication, and evaluation within educational institutions. The study presents a preliminary Research and Development (R&D) design based on the ADDIE model, consisting of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation. Subsequent data collection is planned through needs analysis, expert assessments, practicality questionnaires, observations, and user interviews. The study produces a conceptual framework integrating digital recordkeeping, evidence verification, communication and feedback, data correction, and continuous evaluation. The framework incorporates honesty indicators, including information accuracy, responsible transparency, consistency between reports and supporting evidence, willingness to correct errors, and accountability for decisions. The proposed model also includes user access controls, data modification tracking, and periodic report review mechanisms. The novelty of this study lies in translating honesty values into traceable digital work procedures while incorporating human clarification mechanisms to prevent administrative errors from being automatically interpreted as dishonesty. Since expert validation and field testing have not yet been conducted, the model's feasibility, practicality, and effectiveness remain unverified. Further research is required to validate and test the proposed model with relevant users and experts.

title: ACCESSIBILITY OF ELDERLY CARE SERVICES IN DIGITAL COMMUNITY GOVERNANCE: MECHANISMS, STRUCTURAL BARRIERS, AND INSTITUTIONAL PATHWAYS
summary: The digital transformation of community-based eldercare services has altered the flow of service information and the methods for processing applications. Whether the expansion of digital channels can improve actual service opportunities for older adults depends on the integration of technology with organizational and institutional conditions. This paper employs a comprehensive review of the literature, conceptual analysis, and institutional analysis to define the accessibility of eldercare services as a process-oriented opportunity that spans needs identification, information comprehension, application processing, resource coordination, and service delivery. It constructs an analytical framework in which technology, organization, and institutions jointly shape accessibility. The analysis suggests that information integration, needs identification, resource coordination, support implementation, and feedback-driven course correction constitute the primary mechanisms through which digitalization influences service access. Imbalances between capability requirements and support provision, discrepancies between data categorization and actual needs, disconnects between platform connectivity and accountability, as well as biases in efficiency evaluations, may hinder these mechanisms. New digital barriers may compound economic constraints and supply shortages, while the effectiveness of platform optimization is limited by resource conditions. Governance restructuring aimed at improving accessibility should be guided by actual service access, refining arrangements for channel interoperability, routine assistance, organizational responsiveness, data correction, and equitable evaluation, thereby transforming digital conveniences into inclusive service opportunities.

title: Insights from the U.S. managed care system's primary healthcare framework for capacity building in Chinese community health service institutions — An examination based on comparative institutional analysis and empirical data
summary: After two decades of development, China's community health service system has achieved the phased goal of achieving full institutional coverage; however, the issue of "capacity gaps" has become increasingly prominent. Over the course of four decades, managed care in the United States has evolved into a primary healthcare system centered on the "gatekeeper" model, per-capita payment, performance-based incentives, and clinical pathway management, serving as an important reference for primary healthcare systems worldwide. This paper conducts a multidimensional comparative analysis of the primary healthcare systems in China and the United States, supported by empirical data on healthcare investment, human resource allocation, and service efficiency in both countries. It further examines three representative cases—Kaiser Permanente in the U.S., Luohu District in Shenzhen, China, and Sanming City in Fujian Province, China—through in-depth analysis to explore the institutional logic underlying managed care and its implications for enhancing the capacity of China's community health service institutions. The paper proposes several policy recommendations: reshaping investment mechanisms through the "service procurement" approach; strengthening initial consultation capabilities via the "gatekeeper" function; stimulating endogenous motivation through payment method reforms; and empowering continuous care services through digital transformation.

title: Can organizational image and corporate social responsibility foster citizenship behavior of the employees: a mediational query through organizational identity
summary: Purpose The present research, based upon psychological ownership theory, tries to find out how organizational image and perceived corporate social responsibility (CSR) influence the organizational identity and organizational citizenship behavior (OCB). The present research also tries to find out the role of organisational identity (OI) as a mediator between organizational image and perceived CSR. Design/methodology/approach Survey research using purposive random sampling was conducted in chemical and heavy manufacturing industries in Kolkata, India (N = 243). The survey consisted of a questionnaire measuring the above variables. The data were collected from employees in managerial and supervisory positions. Findings Results were analyzed using SPSS V.25 and Smart-PLS v.4. The mediation model was tested using path analysis. Results show a full mediation effect of organizational identity on the relationship between perceived CSR and OCB and partial mediation of organizational identity on the relationship between organizational image and OCB. Practical implications The results of the present work can have managerial implications. The results of the present research can be used to increase organizational identity and how it can imply a lower attrition rate. Originality/value In today’s scenario, there is an increase in attrition rate especially in emerging economies like India, China and Brazil and there is a need for research to find out what organizational factors are necessary for employees to stay with the organization. The present research tries to find out the psychological mechanism that binds employees to the organization.

title: Maritime Corridor Readiness Under Chokepoint Disruption: A Distributionally Robust Decision Model for Eastern Mediterranean Supply Chains
summary: Maritime chokepoint exposure can be quantified, but supply-chain risk management still requires an ex ante decision about which alternatives to keep ready. The objective is to identify and evaluate an ex ante corridor-readiness portfolio before the disruption state is known, while accounting for shared regional capacity, distributional ambiguity, and tail risk. This study models the Eastern Mediterranean as an interconnected maritime-logistics system comprising five countries, five sectors, five corridors, and six empirically calibrated disruption states. A two-stage distributionally robust decision model couples pre-disruption corridor readiness with post-disruption flow recourse under shared regional capacities, Wasserstein ambiguity, and CVaR tail-risk pricing. Relative to the inferred status quo, the optimized portfolio reduces the composite USD-equivalent objective by USD 241.623 billion, equivalent to 22.6% of the model’s average annual trade-account base under the maintained normalization. This is a calibrated benchmark-distance-to-base ratio, not a realized saving. The optimized portfolio concentrates readiness and improves aggregate performance, yet it performs USD 14.465 billion worse in the Turkish Straits disruption state. Doubling and renormalizing that state’s policy weight shifts the portfolio away from the Turkish Straits and reverses the state-specific loss. The contribution is a transparent decision-analytics framework that places system boundaries, infrastructure interdependencies, advance preparedness, recourse, and residual vulnerability in one auditable supply-chain risk model.

title: The Effect of Green Accounting and ESG on the Value of Mining Companies Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2021 to 2025 Period
summary: This study examines the effect of Green Accounting and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure on the value of mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2021–2025. Using an associative quantitative approach, the study analyzes secondary data obtained from annual and sustainability reports of 25 mining companies selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS 26. Green Accounting was measured using the PROPER index, ESG using the ESG Disclosure Score, and firm value using Tobin's Q. The results indicate that Green Accounting and ESG disclosure have no significant effect on firm value, either partially or simultaneously, with significance values of 0.071, 0.234, and 0.094, all exceeding the 0.05 threshold. The model has limited explanatory power, as reflected by an Adjusted R Square of 2.5%, suggesting that firm value is largely influenced by other factors beyond the variables examined. These findings imply that investors in the Indonesian mining sector continue to prioritize fundamental financial performance and market conditions over sustainability-related information. The negative regression coefficients further suggest that environmental initiatives are still perceived as short-term costs rather than long-term value drivers, highlighting the need for stronger integration of sustainability practices into corporate strategy and reporting.

title: User Empowerment and Perceived System Value in POS Continuance Intention: An SEM–fsQCA Study Among Small Retail Entrepreneurs
summary: Point-of-sale (POS) technology is central to the digital transformation of small retail businesses, yet little is known about the beliefs that keep current users committed to these systems. This study extends the Technology Acceptance Model with perceived system value and user empowerment as antecedents of POS continuance intention, with trust and satisfaction as mediators. Survey data from 196 Thai small retail entrepreneurs with at least six months of POS use were analyzed with covariance-based structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis. User empowerment was the strongest correlate of trust and continuance intention, and its association with continuance intention was almost entirely direct. Perceived system value was consistently associated with satisfaction, but its association with usefulness was not robust across estimators. The associations of usefulness with trust and of satisfaction with continuance intention were not significant, although power to detect them was limited. Both configurations sufficient for high continuance intention combined usefulness, empowerment, and trust, yielding a core that was sensitive to some calibration and threshold choices. Because the sample comprised current users, the design was cross-sectional, and common method variance could not be ruled out, the findings describe associations rather than causes of sustained use. POS providers may benefit from supporting users’ competence and sense of control alongside usefulness and value communication.

title: Transforming strategy with AI and cloud: A case study of dynamic capabilities in action at a Fortune 500 firm
summary: This study examines how a Fortune 500 firm in telecommunications and electronics solutions developed and deployed dynamic capabilities while moving from a hardware-centric model toward AI- and cloud-enabled solutions in response to market and technological shifts. Drawing on the Dynamic Capabilities Framework (DCF), the study is based on a qualitative single-case design, drawing on 22 semi-structured interviews with internal and external participants and documentary sources covering 2019–2024. The findings show that transformation unfolded through three interconnected organizational mechanisms. Ecosystem-embedded sensing enabled the firm to interpret customer, market, technological, and partner signals. Acquisition-led seizing translated those signals into AI/cloud investments, external capability integration, role redesign, and partner-facing solutions. Distributed transforming embedded new digital practices through restructuring, workforce reskilling, cultural adaptation, and collaboration routines across internal units and external relationships. The study contributes to dynamic capabilities and digital transformation literature by clarifying how established DCF dimensions operate at organizational and external-relationship levels during AI- and cloud-enabled transformation. Its contribution lies in explaining capability renewal under legacy constraints. The findings offer practical insights for managers coordinating AI/cloud transformation through sensing routines, acquisition integration, workforce development, and partner enablement.

title: MANAGEMENT OF THE COMPANY'S STRATEGY IN THE CONTEXT OF THE FINANCIAL ASPECT, PRODUCTION AND MARKETING COMPONENTS
summary: The article identifies the financial strategy of an innovative enterprise as a specific object of strategic management under conditions of economic instability, digital transformation, increasing uncertainty, and intensified competition. The main objectives of the financial strategy are identified, including ensuring liquidity and solvency, optimizing profitability, maintaining financial security, managing financial risks, and maximizing enterprise value. The study systematizes the specific features of financial management of innovative enterprises, including high uncertainty and risk, significant resource intensity of research and development, substantial capital requirements, uncertainty of market demand, difficulties in forecasting payback periods, the need to create financial reserves, and continuous reinvestment of profits to maintain technological advantages. The classification of financial strategies according to the stages of the enterprise life cycle is substantiated. It is determined that accelerated growth requires a strategy of financial support for development, sustainable growth requires a strategy of financial provision for stable development, while maturity, decline, or crisis conditions require an anti-crisis financial strategy aimed at ensuring financial security and restoring financial stability. The place of financial strategy within the strategic set of an innovative enterprise is determined. Its integrating role in coordinating corporate, innovation, production, marketing, and other functional strategies is substantiated. The practical significance of the results lies in the possibility of applying the proposed approaches to improve strategic financial management, optimize capital structure, select appropriate sources of innovation financing, manage financial risks, and adapt the financial architecture of an enterprise to changes in its life cycle. Further research should focus on developing methodological approaches to assessing the effectiveness of financial strategies at different stages of innovation projects and improving risk management instruments.

title: ARCHITECTURAL-ADAPTIVE STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT OF ENTERPRISES WITHIN THE TOURISM AND RECREATION COMPLEX
summary: The article substantiates an architectural-adaptive approach to the strategic management of enterprises within the tourism and recreation complex under conditions of a dynamic and uncertain external environment, digital transformation, changing consumer demand and increasing risks. The proposed approach integrates strategic monitoring, analytical diagnostics, scenario modelling, strategic choice, strategy implementation, performance evaluation and adaptive adjustment into a single management cycle. This architecture ensures continuous interaction between the components of strategic management and enables enterprises to revise strategic priorities in response to changes in the external and internal environment. To assess the level of implementation of the proposed approach, the Architectural-Adaptive Maturity Index for Strategic Management (AAMI) is developed. It comprises seven interrelated components: monitoring capability, analytical maturity, scenario readiness, managerial flexibility, organisational integration, digital support and feedback effectiveness. The integral index is calculated as a weighted sum of normalised component values. For the initial testing of the methodology, equal weights are applied. The index makes it possible to determine the overall maturity level of the strategic management system and identify the components that constrain its adaptability. The methodology was tested through an expert assessment of nine enterprises representing different segments of the tourism and recreation complex of Odesa region. The average integral index was 0,717 corresponding to a medium level of architecturaladaptive maturity. Three enterprises demonstrated a high level and six a medium level. The greatest variation was observed in digital support, scenario readiness and managerial flexibility, while organisational integration showed the lowest variability. The results confirm that enterprises with similar integral scores may have different maturity profiles and therefore require different strategic improvement measures. The proposed index can be used for comprehensive strategic diagnostics, comparative assessment, identification of priority areas for improving strategic management systems, and periodic monitoring of their development. Further research should focus on empirical verification of the index, refinement of indicators and weighting coefficients, and expansion of the sample of enterprises.

title: ECONOMIC DIAGNOSTICS OF BUSINESS PROCESSES IN THE REENGINEERING SYSTEM OF HIGH-TECH ENTERPRISES
summary: The article analyzes the significance of economic diagnostics in the system of business process reengineering at high-tech enterprises under conditions of digital transformation and increasing environmental uncertainty. The essence of a business process is clarified as a set of interconnected intellectual, organizational, informational, and technological activities aimed at transforming knowledge and intellectual capital into economic value. A methodological approach to economic diagnostics is proposed, based on a comprehensive assessment of business process performance, economic and time efficiency, resource utilization, digitalization, intellectualization, and adaptability. The approach includes indicator normalization, determination of weighting coefficients, and calculation of an integral index for identifying inefficient processes and evaluating their transformation potential. A matrix approach to prioritizing business processes for reengineering according to economic inefficiency and strategic importance is substantiated. This enables enterprises to identify processes requiring radical transformation, gradual improvement, outsourcing, elimination, or maintenance. A business process reengineering mechanism is developed, providing a sequential transition from diagnostics and identification of critical processes to AS-IS and TO-BE modelling, process redesign, digital and intellectual transformation, and evaluation of results. Special attention is paid to the use of artificial intelligence, Big Data, cloud technologies, robotic process automation, digital platforms, and decision-support systems as tools for business process transformation. It is established that economic diagnostics should assess not only operational efficiency and costs but also the ability of business processes to generate added value, utilize intellectual capital, and adapt to changing conditions. The integration of economic diagnostics and business process reengineering provides a basis for improving resource utilization, increasing process efficiency and adaptability, strengthening digital maturity, and enhancing the competitiveness of high-tech enterprises. Further research should focus on testing the proposed approach and evaluating the economic effects of reengineering initiatives.

title: What Factors Shape the Responsible AI in Accounting and Auditing - Evidence from Japan
summary: This study investigates the interrelationships among generative AI risk assessment, AI policies, AI governance, and adoption practices using survey data from CPAs and corporate accountants in Japan. The analysis on a total of 372 valid responses show that AI governance, AI risk awareness, and training programs emerge as critical for mitigating risks and maximizing efficiency gains. Inadequate AI governance can exacerbate risks. Future responsible AI practices should focus on the need for structured AI policies and enough training systems. This study provides actionable insights for policymakers and practitioners seeking to integrate generative AI into accounting and auditing responsibly.

title: Human–AI Collaboration in Higher Education: Faculty Readiness and Institutional Transformation—A Semantic Review and Bibliometric Mapping
summary: Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is changing how academic work is planned, produced, assessed, communicated, and governed. Yet adoption is uneven: individual faculty members may experiment with AI while institutional workload models, assessment systems, professional development, and governance remain largely unchanged. This paper examines how human–AI collaboration, faculty readiness, and institutional change interact in higher education. Drawing on a semantic synthesis of literature already cited in the supplied data, the paper organises relevant work around five connected themes: AI literacy and faculty capability; task-level human–AI collaboration; professional identity and trust; organisational culture and change capability; and responsible governance. It proposes a transparent protocol for future bibliometric mapping. Importantly, this is a conceptual semantic review, not a completed database-based bibliometric study: no publication counts, co-citation networks, or keyword frequencies are reported as empirical findings. The synthesis suggests that faculty readiness is multidimensional and cannot be reduced to tool familiarity. It includes pedagogical judgement, critical evaluation of AI outputs, ethical awareness, disciplinary adaptation, and confidence to disclose and contest AI-supported decisions. Institutional change requires leadership, protected development time, policy clarity, peer learning, workload recognition, assessment redesign, and participatory governance. A conceptual framework links institutional conditions to faculty readiness, the quality of human–AI collaboration, and feedback into organisational strategy. The paper offers a practical readiness matrix and implementation pathway for higher education institutions, including Indian institutions navigating digital transformation. title: Standardized Preprocedure Protocolling of Stereotactic Breast Biopsies Enables Device-Level Supply Chain Forecasting: A Multisite Quality Improvement Analysis
summary: Background: Breast imaging depends on single-use, vendor-proprietary consumables produced by a concentrated set of manufacturers. During supply shortages in 2026, healthcare organizations faced urgent pressure to shift from reactive to proactive inventory management. Stereotactic breast biopsy needle shortages revealed that traditional forecasting based on procedure volume lacks the granularity needed for device-specific demand. We aimed to enable device-level forecasting through standardized preprocedure protocolling. Methods: In a retrospective analysis of 1,456 stereotactic biopsies across 4 breast imaging sites (June 2025 to June 2026), compliance with a standardized electronic protocolling tool that captured lesion count and needle size (standard vs. petite) was assessed. Compliance rates across sites were compared using chi-square analysis, monthly trends were tracked using run charts, and root cause analysis was conducted to identify barriers at the lowest performing site. Epic reports operationalized protocolled data into historical use tracking and 30-day forward demand forecasts. Results: The overall protocolling compliance rate was 62.7% (913 of 1,456 cases), with striking variation across sites. Specifically, sites A-C achieved 97.3-99.2% compliance, whereas site D (the highest volume site, with 57 cases per month) achieved only 23.4% compliance (c² = 865.7, p < 0.001). Site D remained the lowest performer in all 12 months, indicating systematic workflow failures rather than random variation. Among 913 protocolled cases, the needle mix was 897 standard and 68 petite. Protocolling enabled advance device-demand visibility for about 98% of volume at compliant sites versus only about 23% at site D. Conclusions: Routine preprocedure protocolling converts radiologist planning into structured demand data that can be queried, enabling proactive device-level forecasting that is invisible to traditional case-count methods. This capability directly supports supply chain resilience during shortages. The practice will sustain improvements through monthly compliance monitoring and rolling 30-day demand forecasts. The next improvement cycle will address root causes of protocolling gaps at the noncompliant site and evaluate mandatory protocolling fields to prevent missed protocols.

title: Corporate Governance and Sustainability Disclosure in Environmentally and Socially Sensitive Industries
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how corporate governance relates to environmental and social sustainability disclosure in environmentally and socially sensitive industries and whether these relationships differ from low‐impact industries. Drawing on stakeholder–agency and resource dependence theories, we analyze 3276 firm‐year observations from 503 European Union‐listed firms during 2011–2021 using OLS, instrumental‐variable, and two‐step system‐GMM estimations. Board size and gender diversity are positively associated with both disclosure dimensions. Board independence is positively associated with social disclosure, whereas CEO duality is negatively associated with social disclosure. Supplementary analysis of 6097 observations from 965 firms shows that most relationships between governance and disclosure do not differ significantly by industry sensitivity. However, CEO duality has a significantly more negative association with social disclosure in sensitive industries than in low‐impact industries. These findings identify industry sensitivity as a selective boundary condition and underscore the need to distinguish environmental from social disclosure when evaluating board effectiveness.

title: The Impact Of Adhering to Corporate Governance Standards on Enhancing Decision-making Efficiency:A field Study on publicly traded Companies in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
summary: AbstractObjective: This study aimed to examine the impact of adherence to corporate governance standards in their various dimensions (transparency and disclosure, board independence, effectiveness of audit committees, protection of shareholders’ rights, and accountability and control) on the efficiency of decision-making in joint-stock companies in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.Methodology: The study employed the descriptive-analytical approach, using the questionnaire as the primary tool for collecting primary data from a stratified random sample of (357) respondents working in senior and middle management positions in joint-stock companies listed on the Saudi Stock Exchange, distributed across various economic sectors. The data were statistically processed using SPSS software, employing several statistical methods, including arithmetic means and standard deviations, Cronbach’s alpha coefficient, Pearson correlation coefficient, and both simple and multiple linear regression analyses.Results: The study revealed a high level of corporate governance implementation across its dimensions, as well as a high level of decision-making efficiency in Saudi joint-stock companies. The findings confirmed the existence of a statistically significant impact at the (α ≤ 0.05) level of adherence to corporate governance standards in their combined dimensions on decision-making efficiency, with these dimensions explaining (78.1%) of the variance in the dependent variable. The accountability and control dimension ranked first in terms of impact strength, followed by audit committee effectiveness, transparency and disclosure, board independence, and finally protection of shareholders’ rights.Recommendation: The study recommended strengthening the internal accountability system, developing disclosure mechanisms to include non-financial dimensions, enhancing audit committee efficiency, employing modern technologies to support decision-making, and building an integrated information system connecting various departments within the company.

title: SpectralGuard: a Spectrally grounded λ-SHAP framework for XAI validity certification in pharmaceutical supply chain networks
summary: Permutation-based explainability methods such as SHAP are central to regulatory compliance in AI-governed pharmaceutical supply chains across Sub-Saharan Africa, yet their validity depends on a structural property that existing frameworks do not monitor: the algebraic connectivity of the supply hypergraph, quantified by the Fiedler eigenvalue λ 2 . We prove that λ 2 → 0 is a sufficient condition for permutation-based XAI failure (Theorem 3.5): no increase in sampling effort can recover validity once network connectivity collapses. We introduce SpectralGuard, demonstrated on a calibrated synthetic DGP driven by real Eskom load-shedding and SARB ZAR/USD records ( n = 3, 227 business days, 2014–2026); all spectral results are from the synthetic hypergraph. λ-SHAP shrinks attributions toward a fluid-regime prior using λ 2 ( t ) as the shrinkage weight, maintaining auditability at an explicit bias–variance cost (Remark 3.12). A probabilistic validity certificate V ( t ) combines four spectral metrics with SHA-256 tamper-evidence. An oracle experiment ( B = 500, Seed = 2,026) demonstrates 70.4–89.2% attribution MSE reduction across governance regimes. The spectral gate is the decisive ablation component. In the synthetic DGP, early-warning detection leads classical baselines by 19 business days (λ c alert preceding the λ m crossing). Field validation on real CCMDD procurement data is planned for 2027 (PLMIF-2). A nine-step DHIS2 integration pathway supports SDG 3, 9, 13, and 16.

title: The Influence of Voluntary Environmental Disclosure on the Environmental Impact of Waste Reduction Activities
summary: ABSTRACT Using the Attention Based View (ABV) as a theoretical framework, this study investigates the moderating influence of firm voluntary environmental disclosure on the effectiveness of waste avoidance and waste management to improve two environmental metrics that have received differing levels of attention: carbon emissions and water usage. Employing a panel fixed effects estimation strategy, the results provide two key findings: (1) differing effectiveness of waste reduction strategies to reduce environmental harm and (2) voluntary disclosure moderates the effectiveness of waste reduction strategies to reduce environmental harm, though not always beneficially. Voluntary disclosure improves the environmental benefit of waste avoidance while attenuating that of waste management. Moreover, the moderating influence is more pronounced for water usage, showing that concerns receiving less external attention may benefit more from internal changes in managerial attention.

title: Cybersecurity Strategy and Spoofing Outcomes in Public Corporate Finance in the United States of America
summary: Spoofing attacks exploit trusted digital identities and can expose financial organizations to fraud and operational disruption. Guided by game theory, this quantitative, cross-sectional correlational study examined associations among information security maturity, cybersecurity strategy selection, and self-reported spoofing outcomes in corporate public finance setting. A purposive sample of 93 experienced IT and cybersecurity professionals completed an adapted electronic survey. Pearson correlations showed positive associations between information security maturity and favorable financial outcomes, r(91) = .282, p = .006, and incident-change outcomes, r(91) = .217, p = .037. Cybersecurity strategy selection was also associated with favorable financial outcomes, r(91) = .405, p < .001, and incident-change outcomes, r(91) = .341, p < .001. Maturity and strategy selection were positively associated, r(91) = .640, p < .001. Higher outcome scores represented lower perceived losses or greater reported decreases in incidents. Findings suggest that reported organizational security capabilities and strategic practices covary with more favorable spoofing outcomes. For cybersecurity vendors and public-sector buyers, the findings point to the value of pairing technical controls with measurable organizational readiness and verified outcomes. Interpretation is limited by self-reporting, ordinal outcome measures, nonprobability sampling, uncertainty about organizational clustering, and incomplete documentation of composite scoring. The findings support further investigation of coordinated cybersecurity management using verified incident and financial records, clearly specified measures, and longitudinal designs.

title: INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA OTIMIZAÇÃO DO SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT
summary: Este estudo analisou as contribuições da Inteligência Artificial (IA) para a otimização do Supply Chain Management (SCM), considerando suas aplicações, benefícios e desafios em organizações industriais e logísticas. A pesquisa adotou abordagem qualitativa, de natureza bibliográfica, com finalidade exploratória e descritiva. O levantamento concentrou-se em publicações de 2021 a 2026, localizadas na Scientific Electronic Library Online (SciELO), Portal de Periódicos da Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior (CAPES), Scopus e Google Acadêmico. A análise foi organizada nas categorias aplicações da IA no SCM, contribuições para a tomada de decisões, benefícios e desafios de adoção. Os resultados indicaram possibilidades de utilização em previsão de demanda, estoques, compras, transporte e planejamento, com contribuições para maior capacidade analítica e antecipação de situações operacionais. Também foram identificados desafios relacionados à qualidade dos dados, integração de sistemas, infraestrutura, investimentos e qualificação profissional. Concluiu-se que a IA contribui para a otimização do SCM quando sua utilização está integrada aos processos e às decisões organizacionais.

title: Climate Risk and Sustainable Finance: Bridging Policy, Research and Practice
summary: The implications of climate change and the transition to a low-carbon economy extend to the economy and the financial system, making them increasingly relevant issues for central banks and supervisors. Their complexity makes the exchange of knowledge and experience among experts, academics and central bankers particularly important. Such dialogue helps enrich analysis and advance our understanding and management of risks that continue to pose significant analytical and data-related challenges. With the aim of fostering this exchange, on 25 March 2026, the Banco de España organised the high-level conference “Climate Risk and Sustainable Finance: Bridging Policy, Research and Practice”, together with the Network for Greening the Financial System, the Centre for Economic Transition Expertise and the Transition Pathway Initiative Centre at the London School of Economics. Many of the contributions presented at the conference have been brought together in Issue 33 of Papeles de Energía. This Banco de España publication brings together these contributions, offering different perspectives on the key challenges posed by climate change and the transition for the economy and the financial system.

title: How does patient capital shape ESG performance? Evidence from China
summary: Amid growing emphasis on sustainable development, this study examines the role of patient capital in shaping corporate ESG performance. Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2023, we construct an equity-based patient capital measure capturing shareholdings of active long-term institutional investors. The results show that patient capital is significantly positively associated with ESG performance, and the findings remain robust to a range of alternative specifications and endogeneity tests. Mechanism analyses are consistent with patient capital operating through long-term support, strategic guidance and governance enhancement, corresponding to the environmental, social and governance dimensions. Further analyses reveal strong context dependence. The positive association is more pronounced in firms with stronger development foundations, innovation capacity and governance quality, but weaker in firms facing transition constraints or governance distortions. Overall, this study offers empirical evidence and policy implications for using long-term capital to support green transformation and high-quality development.

title: Mining latent interaction patterns of global LNG maritime logistics networks: A multi-indicator-based link prediction method for marine transport engineering
summary: Detecting emerging ties in shipping network is essential for capturing changes in global trade patterns and enhancing supply chain resilience. This study proposes a multi-indicator coupled link prediction framework integrating network topology, node attributes, and external features to accurately predict potential links in the Liquedied Natural Gas (LNG) shipping network. As a case study of the LNG shipping network from 2018 to 2023, the results show that the method can effectively identify potential LNG shipping links, with a six-year mean Area under the curve (AUC) of 98.19%, a six-year mean accuracy of 98.13%, and a six-year mean precision of 97.3%. The detected emerging transportation ties reveal that LNG shipping is moving a pattern of diversified supply sources, concentrated demand, and strong cross-regional connectivity. These findings provide support for LNG route planning, hub construction, supply-chain risk management, and energy security enhancement.
