title: Novel index on the propensity for digital transformation in agriculture (PADiTIndex)
summary: Abstract Digital agriculture is one of the levers that will enable food systems to adapt and remain resilient in the face of climate change. However, in addition to being generally slow to take off, its adoption is not geographically uniform. While studies at the producer level have investigated the rationale for this disparity, we argue that it could be that different countries and markets are prepared to absorb digital technologies into their value chains. This study assesses the propensity of different countries and markets to digitally transform their agriculture using a new proposed index named Propensity for Agricultural Digital Transformation Index (PADiTIndex) . It uses four indicators including the economic weight of agriculture in the country’s economy, the vulnerability/resilience of the country’s agricultural sector to climate change, the country’s agricultural productivity, and its openness to innovation. To this end, time series data for these four indicators were collected from FAOSTAT, ND- GAIN, USDA and WDCR for the period 2015–2022, making the assessment scalable. A few cases of missing data were completed by interpolation while normalization was used to transform the four indicators that were in different units into a single comparable format. The results indicate that the value of agricultural production per agricultural worker, the resilience of food systems to climate change, and national openness to innovation are the country-level dimensions most closely associated with the propensity of economies to digitally transform their agriculture. In this regard, the Netherlands, Israel, Belgium, Denmark, and Luxembourg stand out as the top five countries where the digital transformation of agriculture is most evident. Conversely, the five countries with the lowest rankings are in Africa (Niger, Madagascar, Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, and Guinea), suggesting room for improvement, beginning with fostering a stronger commitment to modernizing their agricultural sectors to enhance their resilience. This work also corroborates findings from studies, highlighting the well-documented importance of socioeconomic factors in climate change adaptation planning.

title: Transformasi Digital Hijau untuk Keberlanjutan UMKM: Tinjauan Integratif Kapabilitas Digital, Inovasi Hijau, dan Orientasi Kewirausahaan
summary: Digital transformation has expanded the market reach and operational flexibility of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), yet digital adoption does not automatically produce sustainable business outcomes. This study aims to synthesize recent evidence on how digital capabilities, green entrepreneurial orientation, and green innovation interact in strengthening MSME sustainability. An integrative literature review was conducted on 27 peer-reviewed studies published during 2021–2025 and selected through relevance screening of recent literature on digital transformation, green entrepreneurship, green innovation, and sustainable SME performance. The studies were coded by research focus, method, geography, mechanism, and performance outcome. The synthesis shows that digital capability functions primarily as an enabling resource, while green entrepreneurial orientation provides strategic direction and green innovation converts digital resources into economic, environmental, and social value. The relationship is strengthened by digital leadership, stakeholder pressure, government support, access to finance, and organizational readiness, but can weaken when digital investment exceeds absorptive and managerial capacity. The study proposes an integrated digital-green entrepreneurship framework and recommends that MSME digitalization programs shift from technology adoption targets toward capability building, green innovation projects, and measurable triple-bottom-line outcomes.

title: Demand information sharing strategies in supply chains with green services and consumer-to-manufacturer
summary: Abstract This paper constructs a game-theoretical model to investigate demand information sharing strategies in a supply chain consisting of a single manufacturer and a green service platform, while considering the manufacturer’s adoption of the Consumer-to-Manufacturer (C2M) strategy. The green service platform determines whether to disclose demand information. If the platform discloses information, the manufacturer may adopt the C2M strategy to adjust pricing and product decisions based on the shared demand information. We analyze three decision scenarios: no information sharing and no C2M, information sharing and no C2M, and information sharing and C2M. Different from conventional studies that focus on pricing or operational decisions alone, this work innovatively integrates platform green services, demand information asymmetry, and C2M into a unified analytical framework, revealing how C2M strategy efficiency reshapes the platform’s information sharing incentives and the supply chain’s operational outcomes. Contrary to traditional wisdom, our results show that the platform is inclined to share demand information when C2M investment efficiency is at a moderate level. Adopting the C2M strategy can incentivize the platform to share information, thereby creating a mutually beneficial outcome for both supply chain members. We further quantify the impacts of information sharing and C2M strategy choices on consumer surplus and social welfare, which depend closely on C2M investment efficiency. This study fills the research gap regarding the interactive mechanism among platform green services, demand information sharing, and the C2M strategy, and enriches the theoretical system of supply chain information management and digital business model research.

title: DO GREEN ACCOUNTING PRACTICES IMPROVE PROFITABILITY? DYNAMIC PANEL EVIDENCE FROM INDONESIA'S HEALTHCARE SECTOR
summary: This study investigates whether green accounting practices improve the profitability of hospitals listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. The study uses secondary data from eight IDX-listed hospitals over 2019–2024, comprising 96 firm–semester observations. Profitability was measured by using return on assets (ROA) and return on equity (ROE). The explanatory variables on this study are waste generation, electricity consumption, water usage, corporate social responsibility (CSR), and firm size. This study applies a dynamic panel Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) model to address potential endogeneity and unobserved heterogeneity. The findings show that waste generation, electricity consumption, and water usage negatively affect both ROA and ROE, whereas CSR and firm size significantly enhance profitability. The dynamic specification confirms persistence in profitability among IDX-listed hospitals, emphasizing that sustainability practices can reinforce financial resilience.

title: The Impact of Environmental Social Governance for Sustainable Development Goals to BTN Mutual Fund Investment Performance
summary: Introduction: The aim of Investment is for obtaining profits in the future. Sustainable mutual fund is a choice as a major force across global financial markets. Sustainable business growth is not only measured by financial aspects but also measured by the positive impact that generates to the environment and society, which can enhance the competitiveness of the company. It is now common to conduct ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) scoring for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) against mutual fund stocks to obtain mutual funds that are environmentally friendly, and legally safe, with the goal of social welfare. Objective: Understanding the impact of environmental social governance (ESG) and sustainable development goals (SDGs) on the performance and profitability of BTN mutual fund investment products. Research Methods: Cohort/Time series research that describes the performance and profitability of BTN mutual fund products that is chosen by investors, based on secondary data from BTN's ongoing reports. The impact of environmental, social governance (ESG) and sustainable development goals (SDGs) on the performance and profitability of BTN mutual fund investment products is analyzed descriptively and quantitatively using multiple linear regression analysis in SPSS. Novelty: Applied ESG screening/social environmental governance for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), in the management and selection of mutual fund investment products, which will result in increased performance and profitability of low-risk, environmentally friendly, and safe mutual funds. Conclusion. The sustainability score and various pillars of the ESG score for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) have a positive impact on the performance and profitability of BTN mutual fund investments.

title: The Impact of Supply Chain Risk Management on Service Availability and Disruption Reduction: A Field Study on Government-owned Companies in The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
summary: AbstractObjective: This study aimed to investigate the impact of supply chain risk management, with its four dimensions (risk identification, risk assessment, risk response, and risk monitoring and control), on service availability and disruption mitigation in Saudi governmental institutions.Methodology: The study adopted the descriptive analytical approach, and the study population consisted of employees in Saudi government institutions who have a direct connection to supply chain management and service delivery operations. The questionnaire was used as the main tool for data collection, and it was applied to a simple random sample of (336) individuals from employees at the supervisory, middle and senior administrative levels who have a direct connection to supply chain management in Saudi government institutions.Results: The study revealed a statistically significant impact at the significance level (α ≤ 0.05) of supply chain risk management dimensions, both collectively and individually, on service availability and disruption mitigation. These dimensions collectively explained (71.8%) of the variance in the dependent variable. Risk response emerged as the most influential dimension, followed by risk assessment, risk monitoring and control, and finally risk identification. The study also found that the overall level of risk management practices and service availability in Saudi governmental institutions was high.Recommendation: The study recommended enhancing risk response practices, developing assessment methodologies, establishing real-time monitoring systems, expanding digital transformation in government service delivery, fostering a risk-aware organizational culture, and strengthening collaboration with partners and suppliers, all in support of achieving the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030.

title: Communicating for Resilience: Risk Communication and Community-Based Disaster Preparedness through The Corporate Social Responsibility Program of Pt Pertamina Patra Niaga Fuel Terminal Poso
summary: Disaster preparedness requires not only access to risk information but also effective communication, community participation, and multi-stakeholder collaboration. This study aims to analyze risk communication practices in the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) program Disaster Response School implemented by PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Fuel Terminal Poso in Moengko Village, Poso Regency, Central Sulawesi. The study employs a qualitative descriptive approach, with data obtained through in-depth interviews with six informants representing the company, village government, Disaster Preparedness Team, disaster management agency, school, and community, as well as program documentation. The results indicate that risk communication is conducted through face-to-face awareness sessions, visual media, interactive training, and evacuation simulations. This approach provides participants with the opportunity to understand safety procedures and practice basic preparedness skills. Community involvement in determining evacuation routes and safety needs also highlights the importance of two-way communication that bridges technical knowledge with local experience. Collaboration among the company, government, school, and community supports program implementation, while the local philosophy of Sintuwu Maroso, which emphasizes unity and togetherness, serves as a relevant cultural context for collective preparedness. However, several challenges remain, including equitable participation, training continuity, coordination of information updates, and the maintenance of safety facilities and institutional capacity as CSR support is reduced or comes to an end. This study underscores the importance of sustainable, participatory, and risk communication adapted to the local context in supporting community-based disaster preparedness. The findings primarily represent the experiences and perceptions of the informants, rather than a measurement of long-term impacts on behavioral change or disaster risk reduction.

title: Gender and climate financing in non-self-governing territories: the case of Western Sahara
summary: Purpose This study aims to address an explicit gap in the literature on climate finance in conflict contexts. This research examines global and regional climate financing laws, incorporating gender and refugee status considering the case of Western Sahara, a non-self-governing territory (NSGT) pending decolonisation. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a qualitative that applies critical content analysis to 30 global and regional (African) climate finance instruments. The analytical lens drew on regulatory ecology (laws) and critical public policy analysis, based on which systematic manual coding was conducted, recording both the presence and form of normative treatment, enabling cross-instrument comparison and the detection of structural regularities. Findings Climate finance laws insufficiently address the intersection of gender, refugee status and conflict, configuring a structural gap between normative discourse and institutional architecture. Although laws and policies proclaim principles of equity, differentiated responsibility and human rights, the institutional architecture systematically reproduces exclusions in conflict contexts, particularly among refugee populations and gender inequalities. Research limitations/implications This study focuses exclusively on law (hard and soft law) and does not analyse technical documents specific to climate finance mechanisms or the other dimensions of regulatory ecology. While recognising their importance and interdependence, this work proposes an advance in theoretical debates on climate finance in conflict-affected and colonially unresolved contexts, leaving the door open for continued exploration through empirical works examining the other dimensions of regulatory ecology. Originality/value The paper addresses an original and underexplored topic by examining climate finance, gender, refugee status and non-self-governing territory status through the case of Western Sahara.

title: Artificial Intelligence in the Digital Economy: Features of Application and Development Prospects
summary: The subject of research — features of application and development of artificial intelligence technologies, which are becoming key in the digital economy. The aim of the work is to determine the level and characteristics of development of artificial intelligence for different countries, as well as its dependence on the participation of state institutions and influence of constant generation of innovations. The article analyzes the state and structure of artificial intelligence market by different segments: by types of technologies, by deployment models, by solutions, by end-users, company size and geography. The work reveals the main trends of market development, identified and argued advantages and possible disadvantages of using these advanced technologies. The research methods include application of general science analysis and synthesis methods, classification and system, methods of grouping and comparison, economic analysis, as well as historical and comparative-legal methods. The results of the study showed that responsible adoption of artificial intelligence technologies becomes crucial for its positive impact on society. The growing demand for digital information technologies should lead to increased demands for accountability and transparency in the development of artificial intelligence technologies, to the development of a legal doctrine on its development at the international level. The findings of the study point to the need for proactive tools to regulate the legal framework of artificial intelligence, through which the process of developing and using artificial intelligence becomes dynamic and responsible, The use of artificial intelligence systems is synchronized with the global goals of social development.

title: Research on Copyright Infringement Determination of Short Videos in the Digital Economy
summary: Short videos have become an essential product of the digital economy, and with their rapid reuse, editing and algorithmic distribution, the traditional rules of copyright infringement are being challenged. What are the causes of infringement in short-video disputes, and when is liability established? Doctrinal Analysis of Chinese Copyright and Tort Law, a Comparison of the Regimes in the United States and the European Union, Public Statistics on Users and Litigation, and four publicly disclosed adjudicated cases are included. A transparent factor-weighting index will be used to assign weights to the degree of access, similarity, market substitution and permitted use. The indices for the four disputes are all relatively high, ranging from 0.875 to 1.000, but the outcomes on the platform vary among them; some have been dismissed and others found liable. Based on the results, the contested issue is not whether the platform used copies of protected works or whether it was aware of, controlled and profited from the distribution of such works. A Two-Tier Determination Path and Evidence Recommendations for Courts, Platforms and Creators are Proposed.

title: Líneas de defensa empresarial y su impacto en el fraude financiero en pymes ecuatorianas
summary: La presente investigación analiza la incidencia de las líneas de defensa empresarial en la prevención del fraude financiero en pequeñas y medianas empresas (pymes) del sector pesquero de Manta y Portoviejo, Ecuador. En un contexto marcado por alta competencia, limitaciones de recursos y debilidades en los sistemas de control interno, el estudio examina cómo la gestión operativa, la gestión de riesgos y la auditoría interna contribuyen a la reducción de prácticas fraudulentas y al fortalecimiento de la gobernanza corporativa. Se aplicó un enfoque cuantitativo, de alcance correlacional y explicativo, con diseño no experimental y corte transversal. La muestra estuvo compuesta por 32 empresas y 101 participantes, entre gerentes, administradores y responsables financieros. La información se recolectó mediante un cuestionario y se procesó a través de estadística descriptiva, correlación de Pearson y regresión lineal múltiple. Los resultados evidencian una relación positiva y significativa entre las líneas de defensa empresarial y la prevención del fraude financiero (R² = 0.58; p < 0.001). La gestión de riesgos presentó la mayor incidencia explicativa (β = 0.41), seguida de la auditoría interna (β = 0.33) y la gestión operativa (β = 0.28). Asimismo, se constató que las micro y pequeñas empresas muestran mayores debilidades, especialmente en segregación de funciones, gestión de riesgos y auditoría interna. Se concluye que la implementación integral de las líneas de defensa empresarial reduce significativamente la exposición al fraude financiero, fortaleciendo la transparencia, la eficiencia operativa y la sostenibilidad organizacional en las pymes del sector analizado.

title: Institutional technologies and the new frontiers of international marketing and global supply chain management
summary: Purpose This paper introduces the concept of institutional technologies as the socio-technical and interorganizational mechanisms and practices that enable the governance and coordination of economic exchange. We argue that emerging institutional technologies, such as digital platforms, distributed ledgers, smart contracts and digital traceability systems, are reshaping the foundations of international marketing and global supply chain management (SCM) by changing how firms create, substantiate and deliver value across borders. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on a conceptual and integrative approach, this paper examines how emerging institutional technologies alter the conditions under which firms create, substantiate and deliver value propositions and engage in economic exchange. We develop a framework that links institutional technologies to the governance, accountability and legitimacy processes that shape the international marketing–global SCM interface. Findings We argue that institutional technologies are reordering coordination, accountability, legitimacy and value capture across borders. We further suggest that the international marketing–global SCM interface has become a site of joint institutional work, where firms shape technology-enabled standards, proofs and governance arrangements that underpin contemporary cross-border exchange. Building on this perspective, this paper proposes five directions for future research: traceability as a market promise; platformization of international marketing; automation and smart contracts in relation to relational repair; algorithmic coordination as institutional technology; and the interplay between institutional technologies, regulation, geopolitics and infrastructures. We develop five propositions that link each cluster of institutional technologies to the forms of institutional work it performs, the outcomes it influences and the institutional conditions that shape these relationships. Originality/value This paper advances a more technologically grounded understanding of the interface between international marketing and global SCM. It offers a novel conceptual foundation for examining how the technological architectures and governance models of cross-border exchange are being fundamentally recast.

title: RATIO ANALYSIS IN THE AUDIT OF INDUSTRIAL PUBLIC-INTEREST ENTITIES
summary: The article examines coefficient (ratio) analysis as a component of the system of analytical procedures applied in auditing industrial public-interest entities. Despite decades of development of ratio analysis, the issue of establishing reliable normative values for indicators of profitability, liquidity, solvency, financial stability, and business activity remains debatable, especially amid digital technologies enabling processing of large arrays of financial reporting data. The relevance of the topic is reinforced by the war in Ukraine and the transformation of economic processes, which have altered the financial condition of industrial enterprises and the applicability of previously established benchmarks. The purpose of the study is to determine updated normative values of coefficients used by auditors when examining industrial public-interest entities, differentiated by industry and adjusted to current economic conditions. Based on systematization of financial reporting data of Ukrainian large enterprises for 2021–2025, the author identified public-interest entities and calculated average and median values of key indicators for two groups: extractive industry (NACE 05-09) and manufacturing industry (NACE 10-33). Extractive enterprises showed a substantial decline in profitability, liquidity, and financial autonomy, linked to elevated risks of asset loss from military actions. As of 2025, median return on assets for extractive enterprises fell below the inflation rate, indicating an inability to ensure capital reproduction and low attractiveness for investors. Manufacturing enterprises, by contrast, demonstrated positive dynamics in most indicators, reflecting greater adaptability of their business models to crisis conditions. The study substantiates the expediency of applying median rather than average values as more representative benchmarks, since averages may be distorted by enterprises facing bankruptcy risk or significant financial imbalances. The practical significance lies in enabling auditors to form more balanced conclusions about clients' financial condition, considering industry specifics and current economic realities.

title: Prioritizing sustainability indicators in the coffee supply chain via the fuzzy SAW method
summary: Purpose This research identifies, classifies, and prioritizes sustainability indicators for the Colombian coffee supply chain. Given the industry’s challenges and growing international demand, the study aims to enhance supply chain sustainability by analyzing the most relevant variables based on global standards. Design/methodology/approach Indicators selected from a literature review were assessed by experts using a fuzzy scale to address subjectivity. A fuzzy simple additive weighting (SAW) method then employed to prioritize the indicators, with final weights and rankings obtained though Minkowski-base defuzzification. Findings Forty four indicators were refined and evaluated by 15 experts. These indicators were ranked by importance, allowing for their specific prioritization within social, environmental, and economic sustainability dimensions. The results highlight a subset of high impact indicators that are closely linked to productivity enhancement, performance management, and operational decision making across the coffee supply chain. Research limitations/implications The primary limitation of this study pertains to the expert selection process and the collection of Likert-scale assessments. Although 25 experts were initially invited, time constraints prevented full participation. However, the final panel of 15 is considered methodologically sufficient given their extensive expertise in the coffee supply chain. Future research could evaluate methodological alternatives, such as excluding expert weighting or developing novel approaches to assess expert influence. Additionally, other multi-criteria decision-making methods, such as Fuzzy TOPSIS or DEMATEL, warrant further investigation. Practical implications From a practical standpoint, the proposed prioritization offers a performance-oriented decision support tool for stakeholders across the coffee supply chain. Rather than managing extensive and unprioritized indicator sets, coffee growers, cooperatives, industry organizations, and policy makers can use the ranked indicators to focus improvement efforts on high impact variables. Specifically, the results suggest prioritizing investments in productivity enhancing practices, quality and process management, workforce training, soil conservation, and water efficiency. By concentrating managerial actions on the most influential indicators at each stage of the supply chain, practitioners can achieve faster and more effective improvements in sustainability while simultaneously strengthening productivity and overall performance. Originality/value Prioritizing economic, environmental, and social indicators enables the identification of key variables and their impact on outcomes, allowing stakeholders to concentrate improvement actions on the factors most critical to sustainability, productivity, and performance in the coffee supply chain. From an academic perspective, this study contributes to the productivity and performance management literature by operationalizing sustainability through a ranked set of indicators that explicitly link indicator level variables to performance outcomes. Methodologically, the integration of fuzzy SAW, expert weighting, and Minkowski defuzzification provides a structured and replicable performance-oriented decision framework that extends prior sustainability indicator studies within agri-based supply chains.

title: Bright against dark: how supply chain slack influences sustainable performance
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how supply chain slack influences sustainable performance, both directly and indirectly, through the mediating roles of operational resilience, specifically resistance and recovery capacity. It further investigates how environmental complexity conditions these relationships, providing a comprehensive understanding of when supply chain slack contributes to sustainable performance. Design/methodology/approach The analysis is based on a dataset of 2,067 Chinese A-share-listed manufacturing firms during the COVID-19 pandemic. Findings The authors find that supply chain slack has a direct negative effect on sustainable performance and positive indirect effects through the two aspects of operational resilience: resistance and recovery capacity. Furthermore, environmental complexity negatively moderates the direct effect and positively moderates the two indirect effects. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by unveiling the double-edged sword effect of supply chain slack under environmental complexity. It highlights how operational resilience can transform the positive aspects of supply chain slack into sustainable performance, offering a nuanced understanding of the effect of supply chain slack on sustainable performance under environmental complexity.

title: Managing The Supply Chain Behind The Butcher: Purchasing and Procurement Practices at Fast Hotel
summary: This study aims to analyze the role of Purchasing management in the procurement process to support Butcher operations at Fast Hotel and to identify the stages of the procurement process implemented. This study employed a descriptive qualitative approach. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation involving informants consisting of the Purchasing Coordinator, Receiving Staff, and Butcher Staff. Data analysis was conducted through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing and verification. Data validity was assessed using method triangulation by comparing the results of interviews, observations, and documentation. The results show that the role of Purchasing management at Fast Hotel has generally been implemented in accordance with the relevant theoretical framework, covering goods requirement planning, supplier selection, purchasing processes, cost control, quality control, and interdepartmental coordination. The procurement process is also implemented through six stages, namely needs identification, procurement procedures, goods receiving, storage, distribution, and documentation. However, several challenges remain, including supplier delivery delays, discrepancies between the quantity of goods received and the quantities stated in the Purchase Order (PO), and sudden requests from user departments. These challenges may affect the timeliness and continuity of fulfilling the operational requirements of the Butcher department. Therefore, more consistent supplier monitoring, periodic supplier evaluation, more accurate quantity verification, and improved coordination among Purchasing, Receiving, and Butcher are required. Overall, Purchasing management plays an important role in ensuring the availability of raw materials and supporting the smooth operation of the Butcher department at Fast Hotel.

title: Senior Executive Pay and Corporate Sustainability Performance: The Roles of Green Innovation, Governance and State Ownership in China
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the association between senior executive pay and corporate sustainability performance using 14,524 firm‐year observations of Chinese A‐share listed firms over the period 2019–2023. This period provides consistent data availability and encompasses China's transition towards the 2020 dual‐carbon policy. Drawing on agency, managerial power, stakeholder and resource dependence theories, we investigate nonlinear effects, green innovation as a mediating mechanism, and governance and ownership as boundary conditions. We find that senior executive pay is positively associated with sustainability performance, although this association weakens at higher levels of pay. Green innovation partially mediates this relationship, while gender composition, managerial age, overseas experience and board independence condition its strength. The positive association is stronger among state‐owned enterprises, particularly after 2020. These findings remain robust to alternative measures of executive pay, lagged specifications, additional governance controls, propensity score matching and entropy balancing. Overall, the findings suggest that compensation design should account for sustainability objectives, compensation levels, governance characteristics and the broader institutional context.

The key indicators used to assess the level of digitalization (ROI, Cost-to-Income ratio) are analyzed, and scientific proposals and practical recommendations for improving the efficiency of digital transformation in the banking system of Uzbekistan are developed.

title: How IT Architecture Flexibility and Governance Decentralization Shape Digital Transformation Capabilities
summary: Modular systems theory and the dynamic capabilities perspective suggest that modularity in the IT function, both architectural and organizational, shapes a firm’s digital transformation capabilities (DTCs), yet the joint effect of these two organizational-design choices has not been tested. Drawing on survey data from 188 U.S. firms and partial least squares structural equation modeling, this study examines how IT architecture flexibility and IT governance decentralization, separately and jointly, influence digital sensing, digital seizing, and digital transforming. Findings suggest that IT architecture flexibility has strong positive effects on all three dimensions, while IT governance decentralization positively affects sensing and seizing but not transforming. Crucially, the interaction between flexibility and decentralization negatively moderates the relationships with sensing and seizing, indicating that technical and organizational modularity can substitute rather than complement. The study contributes a nine-micro-foundation operationalization of DTCs and challenges the prevailing complementarity assumption between architectural and governance modularity.

title: Where ESG enters the investment process: a systematic review of ESG portfolio research
summary: Portfolio outcomes depend not only on asset characteristics but also on how assets are selected, weighted and evaluated. Mixed findings on environmental, social and governance (ESG) portfolios are commonly attributed to differences in data, models, markets, or rating providers, with less attention to the stage at which ESG first enters the investment process. This study addresses that gap through a PRISMA-based systematic review of 201 included studies – 196 research articles and 5 review articles – combined with bibliometric analysis and directed content analysis. A theory-informed, rule-based codebook was applied to the full texts. Each study received one primary role based on the earliest material ESG entry in its principal analytical design. The final coding classified ESG as a Constraint that changes the investable universe in 51 studies (25.4%), a Mechanism that enters portfolio construction or allocation in 77 studies (38.3%), and Evaluation used to assess investment outcomes or behavior in 73 studies (36.3%). The classification distinguishes asset eligibility, portfolio allocation and investment evaluation as separate decision contexts. It provides a structured basis for organizing the literature and interpreting findings with attention to how ESG is used. Its contribution is descriptive and interpretive: the classification does not establish that differences in ESG entry points cause differences in portfolio returns.

title: Assessing Accounting Interns’ Achievement In Communication Skills
summary: This study examines the impact of internship experiences on the communication competencies of accounting students, specifically analysing self-assessed growth in verbal, written and social communication from pre- to post-internship and final skill achievements. Using descriptive research design, primary data was gathered through a self-administered online survey of 44 accounting interns. The findings demonstrate substantial overall improvement in the students' perceived verbal, written and social communication skills following their internships. The growth was primarily driven by structured workplace interactions such as meetings and task clarifications with supervisors and managers, followed by discussions with colleagues, referencing audit reports and direct client interactions during audit fieldwork. These experiences led to high self-reported achievement across all five communication indicators as every respondent reported their ability to communicate pleasantly and professionally in the workplace. Consequently, these insights highlight the vital role real-world experience plays in developing student communication. It offers valuable guidance for universities to refine their curricula and internship programs to better prepare future accounting professionals.

title: Nonlinear Dynamics of ESG , ESG Controversies, and Firm Performance: The Role of Controlling Shareholders
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the nonlinear relationships between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance, ESG controversies, and firm performance, and investigates the moderating role of controlling shareholders. Using panel data from A‐share listed mainland Chinese firms within Huawei's domestic supplier network from 2018 to 2022, this study applies firm fixed effects models with year fixed effects and firm‐level clustered standard errors. The findings provide weak evidence of a U‐shaped relationship between overall ESG performance and firm performance, while governance performance exhibits the strongest nonlinear relationship. In contrast, environmental and social performance show no significant nonlinear associations with firm performance. ESG controversy exposure also shows no robust nonlinear relationship with firm performance. The moderation results indicate that controlling shareholder influence may flatten the U‐shaped relationship between ESG performance and firm performance, while its moderating role in the ESG controversy relationship remains statistically weak. However, these moderation findings are sensitive to alternative proxies for controlling shareholder influence. Drawing on stakeholder theory and the principal–principal conflict perspective, this study demonstrates that the relationship between ESG performance and firm performance varies across ESG dimensions and may depend on shareholder control. The findings provide implications for managers, investors, and policymakers by emphasizing the importance of considering the nonlinear and governance‐dependent nature of ESG‐related outcomes.

title: Implications of Land-border Closure and Reopening for Food Supply Chains in South-West Nigeria
summary: Background: Land-border restrictions can alter market access and the organisation of regional food distribution. This study describes reported food-price and food-security experiences in South-West Nigeria in the context of Nigeria’s border closure and subsequent reopening. Methods: A cross-sectional field survey in 2025 included 127 respondents. Percentage distributions and exploratory chi-square summaries were analysed. Results: Respondents were predominantly aged 26–45 years (55.9%), and 81.9% reported tertiary education. Following reopening, 37.8% reported no change in food prices, whereas 25.2% reported substantial increases and 18.9% slight decreases. Among 126 classified responses to a retrospective question about closure, 85 participants reported meal reduction or skipping. A separate item asking about shortages when borders were open received 40 “sometimes”, 26 “often”, and 21 “always” responses. The reported chi-square summaries indicate possible associations with education and occupation, but underlying contingency tables are unavailable for independent evaluation. Conclusions: Respondents described heterogeneous experiences of food access and prices; the cross-sectional data do not isolate the causal effect of border policy. Further research with verified individual-level records, consistent item coding and objective market observations is required to establish policy-specific effects.

title: Supply Chain Finance: Designing Supplier Monitoring Incentives for Bank-Financed Retailer Inventory
summary: Bank-funded supply chain finance can support retailers’ inventory purchases, but compensating core suppliers for hidden monitoring effort can reduce lending profits. This study examines how banks should design monitoring incentives for core suppliers that sell inventory to cash-constrained retailers. The contribution of the three-party principal–agent model is to link supplier trading earnings, the retailer’s order and borrowing response, and the bank’s default recovery. Least-cost supplier contracts are derived under participation, incentive and payment-floor constraints, and illustrative financing offers are compared on nested grids. The illustrative results show that baseline financing supports larger retailer orders and higher retailer profits than self-financing, while low monitoring effort is preferred because the additional recovery from high effort is outweighed by its incentive cost. Lower effort costs and more informative signals can make high effort preferable without increasing retailer orders. A common minimum supplier payment reduces bank profitability and, when sufficiently high in the tested scenarios, leads to no financing. These illustrative grid findings support assessing monitoring’s recovery gains against incentive costs and retailer responses; they do not establish a continuous-offer equilibrium.

title: AyurAuth: A Decentralized Edge-AI and Permissioned Blockchain Framework for Herbal Supply Chain Authenticity
summary: Ensuring the provenance and authenticity of raw herbal materials in B2B supply chains requires integratingrapid species verification with immutable record-keeping. Existing centralized systems suffer from single-point trustvulnerability, while public blockchain architectures incur high gas fees and execution delays. This paper presentsAyurAuth, a unified framework combining lightweight Edge-AI species classification using fine-tuned MobileNetV2 with apermissioned Hyperledger Fabric v2.x blockchain ledger. Deployed via a Node.js REST API and Flask microservice,AyurAuth achieves an empirical top-1 leaf classification accuracy of 85.00% (88.6 ms inference latency) across five keyAyurvedic herb species. Benchmark testing via Hyperledger Caliper demonstrates a peak write throughput of 408.47 TPSwith a commit latency of 145.8 ms at 100 TPS, and a read throughput of 485.44 TPS at 41.5 ms latency with 100% successrate. End-to-end batch onboarding completes in 394.4 ms, while buyer QR verification queries execute in 28.5 ms withoutexposing internal ledger credentials.

title: Digital transformation of anxiety and depression in adolescents: Phenomenology, neurobiology, clinical challenges
summary: Although numerous studies have examined digital activity’s impact on mental health, how the digital environment transforms the phenomenology of mental disorders remains insufficiently understood. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on how the digital environment influences the clinical manifestations of anxiety and depression in adolescents. Digital phenomena such as social comparison, fear of missed opportunities, problematic use of social networks and internet games, and doomscrolling not only accompany affective symptoms but also become integral behavioral and cognitive components, serving a dual function: they act as ‘masks’ that complicate diagnosis and as factors contributing to chronicity. The neurobiological ground of this process includes dysregulation of the reward system, overload of the prefrontal cortex, and hyperactivation of the default mode network, which together establish a self-perpetuating cycle of emotional distress, maladaptive digital behavior, and increased distress. Clinically, these findings underscore the importance of incorporating a ‘digital history’ into standard diagnostic interviews and developing integrative therapeutic approaches that address both affective disorders and maladaptive digital behavioral patterns.

title: IMPROVING THE POPULATION'S COMPETENCIES IN USING PUBLIC SERVICES IN THE CONTEXT OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
summary: This article examines the problems associated with public digital literacy in accessing electronic public services, considering the interrelationship between organizational, technological, and social factors. The gap between the availability of digital public services and citizens’ ability to use them independently, effectively, and securely is identified as the central research problem. The main factors contributing to this problem are systematized based on international studies, Uzbekistan’s regulatory and legal framework on digital transformation, and theoretical approaches to the use of electronic services. As a result, the study proposes a step-by-step learning mechanism that integrates the development of citizens’ digital skills into the service delivery process itself. This mechanism includes the stages of independently completing a service, consolidating practical skills, ensuring information security, and incorporating user feedback. The proposed approach aims to reduce difficulties in accessing electronic public services and promote digital inclusion.

title: Supply Chain Disruption Risk and Return on Assets: The Moderating Roles of Disruption Characteristics in Chinese Semiconductor Industry
summary: This paper examines the relationship between supply chain disruption risk (SCDR), three disruption characteristics, and return on assets (ROA) in China’s semiconductor industry. Guided by Event System Theory and dynamic capabilities theory, the study treats the disclosure-based frequency, durability, and familiarity indicators as moderators of the SCDR–ROA relationship. The analysis uses annual-report Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) disclosures and financial data for 92 Chinese A-share semiconductor firms observed from 2021 to 2025, yielding 460 firm-year observations. The integrated ROA moderation model includes SCDR, all three indicators, their three interactions with SCDR, and controls for total assets, employees, and firm age. The direct SCDR path is negative but not significant. The SCDR by frequency-proxy interaction is negative and significant, while the durability and familiarity interactions are not significant in the baseline specification. The frequency-proxy result remains significant under an alternative semantic-similarity threshold. The evidence links denser disruption-related disclosure to a more negative conditional SCDR–ROA association.
